title: pre-commit as a companion, part 2: hooks status/doctor treat a pre-commit-governed repo with ddflow's local hooks as installed; the standards gate can run 'pre-commit run --from-ref <base> --to-ref HEAD'; the install-companions prompt walks it

body: tests/test_help.py unknown_cli_mentions (e1b8a73) passes a nonexistent command: COMMAND_MENTION in services/help.py stops at a hyphen, so the prefix escape any(leaf.startswith(mention+'-')) accepts `ddflow hooks check` because leaf 'hooks check-msg' exists. Probe: unknown_mentions(command_mentions('`ddflow hooks check`')) == []. Found by critic (LAN Qwen).

9b8394d _withdraw_claim forgets the claims left when a release ends a contest and the displayed lease is not the one withdrawn: lease_contest=[] with the rest moved nowhere, so a later claim overlapping one of them is not reported (critic finding 2). Repro via fold: c 1000+1000, r 1500+1000, l 3000+1000 by r's holder, release r (event), then n 1200+1000 -> no contest though c and n overlapped. Same mechanism makes H 4000+1000, R 1000+800, D 1500+1000, release D fold-order dependent (R forgotten in orders R,D,H and D,R,H).

Releasing the DISPLAYED lease while a contest still stands leaves it.lease None (critic finding 3; pre-existing for 2+ contestants left, kept by 9b8394d): A 1000+2000, B 2000+2000, C 3500+1500, release C -> lease None with A and B contested, where the log without C displays B. Also true when a historical contest stands and the displayed (uncontested) lease is released.

_h_resolved clears lease_contest and overwrites the displayed lease without keeping the claims the resolution did NOT release, so they vanish from the record and a later claim overlapping one is not weighed against it (found in bug hunt of the critic fixes; pairwise resolve made it reachable). Repro via fold: X 1000+1000, Y 1900+1000, M 150+150, K 100+100, resolve --keep K (releases M and Y) -> X nowhere, all 24 orders; two-groups case keep alice loses carol in 4 of 24 orders.

complete's independence check labels the critic 'google' though the reviewer is declared family='alibaba' (served name <served-model>, weights <served-model>): it infers the family from the recorded model NAME instead of the gate evidence's declared family. Harmless while the author is anthropic, but a reviewer whose served name hides its true family can pass (or fail) the cross-family rule wrongly. Probe: ddflow complete B-fix-remedy-texts -> "independence": "critic was google vs author anthropic"; its critic evidence has family 'alibaba' (2026-09-29, main 218a681).

Bug B6ed8b9edb8: reviewer_independence (services/gates.py) derives each reviewer's family from the model NAME, so the LAN <served-model> served as <served-model> and declared family='alibaba' in .ddflow/reviewers.toml is reported as 'critic was google'. Prefer evidence['family'] when the evidence came from ddflow review (it also carries 'reviewer'); agents' gate record cannot write a family key, so the declared family stays operator-controlled. Fall back to the name for manual records, or when the family is empty/'unknown'. Regression test: a review-recorded critic with model '<served-model>', family 'alibaba' reads as alibaba; a manual record with the same model still reads google; a declared family equal to the author's is NOT independent (the dangerous direction). Operator 2026-09-29: 'fix the new bug you found and merge with main'.
title: Reviewer independence uses the family ddflow review recorded, not one guessed from the served model name (fixes bug B6ed8b9edb8)

body: 9c288e2 _h_resolved displaces EVERY unreleased contestant by the kept claim, including bystanders that still overlap each other (re-review): a=(900,100) b=(300,100) c=(300,100) d=(100,800) acquired a,d,c,b; resolve --keep a releases only d, then lease_contest [] and displaced [(c,by=a),(b,by=a)] -- contest_summary empty and resolve refuses 'not contested' though unreleased b and c overlap

a73d367 lowercases the declared family but not the author's (family_for returns the map's value verbatim), so with [agent].families mapping to 'Alibaba' a reviewer declared 'ALIBABA' is judged independent of an 'Alibaba' author: 'critic was alibaba vs author Alibaba' (rubber-duck, CONFIRMED)

An agent can fabricate an 'independent' review: MCP ddflow_configure (toml, no operator gate) appends a [[reviewer]] of kind 'command' with an agent-chosen command (e.g. printing 'STATUS: NO FINDINGS') and model/family; ddflow_review then records critic evidence that satisfies the cross-family rule. Pre-existing (reproduced before a73d367 with model='<served-model>'); a73d367 widens it slightly, since a declared family now counts even when the model name is unrecognised. Remedy belongs at the door: reviewer entries (and command reviewers above all) written over MCP need operator approval, or reviews are only trusted from reviewer entries in the operator-owned .ddflow/reviewers.toml. Found by the rubber duck on B-fix-declared-family.

Decision D-roborev-local (operator 2026-09-29). roborev reads .roborev.toml from each checkout and has no machine-local per-repo file, so an untracked copy must reach each worktree. (a) knob [worktree].local_files = [] (repo-relative paths); (b) worktree create copies each existing one from the primary, never overwriting a file already in the worktree, and never a TRACKED path (refuse at config load: a tracked file is not local); (c) status/doctor note a listed file missing from the primary; (d) this repo sets local_files = ['.roborev.toml'] in its git-ignored local config. Test: a new worktree gets the copy; a tracked path is refused.
title: [worktree].local_files: git-ignored machine-local files (e.g. .roborev.toml, .claude/settings.local.json) copied from the primary checkout into every worktree ddflow creates

body: companions reports a companion 'installed but no agent is configured to launch it' when .mcp.json launches it under a different server key: run_nemo_run's .mcp.json has 'coding-guides' running docker.io/delian/codeguide-mcp, yet adopt and 'ddflow companions' say codeguide is not wired up and advise 'companions add --id codeguide', which would register it a second time. Detection matches the server key name, not the launch command/image.

hooks install, refusing over an existing pre-commit hook, tells the operator to add the check-commit line to .git/hooks/pre-commit even when that file carries 'File generated by pre-commit' (run_nemo_run): pre-commit regenerates it on install, so the edit is silently lost. It should detect the pre-commit framework header and advise a local hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml instead (relates to B-precommit-integration).

resolve --keep X widens X's lease to the resolve time (renewed_at = max(renewed_at, at)) but never re-checks the widened window against claims still on record: after A(1150,300), E(1200,300), C(150,150), D(250,50) and resolve(keep=D, at=5000), A (1150-1450) lies inside D's widened 250-5050 window yet sits in displaced with contest []. Pre-existing in kind: main drops such a claim from the record entirely; B-fix-contest-overjoin (8763d92) keeps it on record but misfiles it. Also a modelling question: widening treats a long-lapsed lease as continuously held. Found by the third re-review of B-fix-contest-overjoin (7 random instances, one root cause).

adopt run from inside a linked worktree writes the project's TRACKED files into the PRIMARY checkout (repo_root resolves via --git-common-dir): on run_nemo_run it appended to the primary's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, edited .mcp.json and .gitattributes and created docs/ddflow/, leaving the shared primary dirty while the caller's worktree got nothing. The shared event log belongs in the primary; files meant to be committed through the caller's branch belong in the caller's own tree (--show-toplevel). It also then 'kept' .claude/commands/implement.md because it looked at the primary's copy, not the worktree where it had been deleted.

Every worktree whose branch predates a NEW config knob can no longer commit or run ddflow: the git hook sets PYTHONPATH to the primary but 'python -m ddflow' puts the CWD (the worktree) first on sys.path, so the worktree's OLDER ddflow code loads the primary's NEWER .ddflow/config.toml and Config.load raises 'unknown knob enforce.forbidden_trailers' (after B-forbid-trailers merged, 2026-09-29). Commits are refused for a reason unrelated to them; the workaround is merging main first. Same family as B8ea7a90aea / L-gate-cmd-vs-branch-deps (config from the primary, code from the branch). Fix: run the primary's code in the hook (python -I / an absolute module path), or let an unknown knob degrade to a warning when the config is newer than the code.

A knob added to the shared .ddflow/config.toml breaks every ddflow whose code predates it: Config rejects an unknown knob with ValueError, so after [enforce].forbidden_trailers landed on main (3e6ea58) every running MCP server and every CLI run from a worktree branch that has not merged main fails on EVERY call ('unknown knob enforce.forbidden_trailers'). Config and code are versioned apart (the primary's config is read by all worktrees' code), so an unknown knob must be a doctor warning, not a hard error; strictness belongs in 'config --set' validation. Probe: python3 -m ddflow status from a worktree branch without the knob -> ValueError; from main's code -> works (2026-09-29).

hooks status reports 'pre-commit hook: NOT installed' and 'commit-msg hook: NOT installed -- NOTHING checks it' (exit 2) in run_nemo_run, where both checks ARE armed through the pre-commit framework (.pre-commit-config.yaml local hooks ddflow-check-commit / ddflow-check-msg -> scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit|check-msg; verified: a trailer-less message is refused, a Phase-ships one passes). enforce.installed only looks for HOOK_MARKER in .git/hooks/<name>, which a framework-generated hook never carries. Status should also recognise a .pre-commit-config.yaml hook whose entry runs 'hooks check-commit'/'hooks check-msg' (relates to B695d7925bf).

import --verify crashes with OSError Errno 36 (File name too long) in run_nemo_run: _memory_sources treats any imported lesson/research/decision source containing '/' as a path, and a prose seen_in ('2026-08-21 Phase 136, roborev 414-D4 (and its earlier duplicate ...') reaches (repo / rel).is_file(). The check for unfinished imports (no-globs tasks, shipped drift, vanished sources) has therefore never run there.

trailer check accepts an item id that names no item: 'Phase: NOPE.99' passes check-msg with exit 0 in run_nemo_run, so a mistyped id reaches history and the audit the trailer exists for cannot match it. The retired check_phase_trailer.py was stricter (and checked Phase-ships against its vocabulary none|filing|recon|evidence|followup).

companions: optmem is still default=true and reported missing although ddflow's own memory entity (35dd944, 'ddflow memory add') replaced it, and the memory companion's why still says recall does not cover operational facts. Separately, registered_in matches only the server NAME, so run_nemo_run's .mcp.json entry 'coding-guides' (docker run docker.io/delian/codeguide-mcp) is reported as 'no agent is configured to launch it'.

import --include-done never completes a PHASE: a finished phase (heading '✅ CLOSED', every checkbox ticked) imports as open, so after a history import status shows 0 of 301 phases done in run_nemo_run. And without --include-done a partly-shipped phase (103: 103.A + 103.C ticked and SHIPPED in the heading) shows 0/3 with its shipped tasks absent, with nothing saying they were skipped.

Bug Bd5b59f3894: _memory_sources accepts any source containing '/' as a path; a lesson seen_in that is a sentence reaches (repo/rel).is_file() and raises OSError Errno 36 in run_nemo_run, so verify never ran there. Fix: a source is a path only if it is one path-shaped token (no whitespace, bounded length); and a stat that raises OSError is 'not a path', never a crash or a vanished finding. Regression test: an imported lesson whose seen_in is a >255-char sentence with '/' -- verify_import returns a report; fails on current code with OSError.
title: import --verify never crashes on an imported record whose source is prose, not a path (fixes bug Bd5b59f3894)

body: Bug B259fd32dbd: enforce.installed only finds HOOK_MARKER in .git/hooks/<name>; a pre-commit-framework hook never carries it, so run_nemo_run (ddflow-check-commit / ddflow-check-msg local hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml) is told 'NOT installed ... NOTHING checks it' and exit 2. Fix: a framework-generated hook (the 'File generated by pre-commit' header) whose .pre-commit-config.yaml has a hook at that stage whose entry runs 'hooks check-commit' / 'hooks check-msg' counts as installed, and status says it is armed through pre-commit. Regression test: repo with such a config + generated hooks -> status reports both installed, exit 0; fails on current code.
title: hooks status recognises ddflow checks armed through the pre-commit framework (fixes bug B259fd32dbd)

body: Bug B438d336b24: 'Phase: NOPE.99' passes check-msg. Fix: the value of an item_trailer_keys trailer must be the id of an item in the queue (not removed); new [enforce].trailer_waivers = {key = [words]} declares keys that mark a commit shipping no item (run_nemo_run: Phase-ships = none|filing|recon|evidence|followup), whose value must be one of those words. A queue that cannot be read is exit 2 (could not run), never a pass. run_nemo_run's config gets the waiver map in the same change window. Regression test: NOPE.99 refused naming the key and value; a real id passes; Phase-ships: none passes with the waiver, Phase-ships: bogus refused; fails on current code.
title: The item trailer must name an item in the queue; a waiver key takes only its declared words (fixes bug B438d336b24)

body: Bug B45d5aa72fa: the importer never completes a phase. With --include-done a phase whose every imported task is done/closed (or that has no tasks and whose heading carries the done marker) must be imported completed with evidence naming the source; a phase with open tasks stays open. Without --include-done, the report must say how many ticked tasks per phase were left out so '0/3' is not read as 'nothing shipped'. Also a re-run of --include-done over an existing import must add the missing done tasks under existing phases (103.A/103.C under 103). Regression test on a fixture with a CLOSED phase, a partly-shipped phase and an open one; fails on current code.
title: import --include-done completes a finished phase; a plain import says which ticked tasks it left out (fixes bug B45d5aa72fa)

body: Bug B52751f12ed: optmem default=true and flagged missing though 'ddflow memory' (35dd944) does its job; the memory companion's why says recall does not cover operational facts. registered_in matches only the name, so '.mcp.json: coding-guides -> docker run docker.io/delian/codeguide-mcp' reads as unregistered. Fix: optmem default=false with a why that points at ddflow memory; memory companion text current; registered_in also matches an entry whose command+args equal the companion's launch (and reports the name it is registered under). Regression tests for both; fail on current code. Waits on B-precommit-companion (holds companions.toml/.py) per operator 2026-09-29.
title: Companions: OptMem no longer a default (ddflow memory replaced it), and a server registered under another name is found by its launch command (fixes bug B52751f12ed)

body: doctor's duplicate_work warns that two items with identical globs 'cannot run in parallel' even when one already needs the other (run_nemo_run KNOWNFAIL.2 needs KNOWNFAIL.1): the dependency already serialises them, so the warning asks the operator to act on nothing. core/progress.py _duplicate_work groups by globs without looking at needs (transitively).

Bug Bd1c601896f: _duplicate_work groups live items by identical globs and warns 'cannot run in parallel' even when one item needs the other (directly or transitively), e.g. run_nemo_run KNOWNFAIL.2 needs KNOWNFAIL.1. Fix: within a same-globs group, drop the finding when the items are totally ordered by needs; keep it for any pair that is not ordered. Regression test: two same-glob items, one needing the other -> no duplicate_work; two unordered -> still flagged; fails on current code.
title: doctor's duplicate_work does not flag a pair whose dependency already orders them (fixes bug Bd1c601896f)

body: [worktree].local_files is not copied into a tree claim binds without W.create: the harness tree adopted via W.current (adopt_existing) and the item's recorded tree on a re-claim (lifecycle.claim rebind). The knob doc promised 'creates or adopts'. Fix needs ddflow/api/lifecycle.py (held by B-wait-wake). Found by roborev/kilo on LAN <served-model>.

copy_local_files lets an OSError from shutil.copy2 (unreadable source, ENOSPC) escape W.create; lifecycle.claim catches only GitError, so the claim dies with a traceback after the worktree exists but before worktree.created is recorded. Found by roborev/kilo on LAN <served-model>.

Found by the cross-family review of B-worktree-local-files. lifecycle.claim binds a tree in three ways; only the W.create path copies [worktree].local_files. Move the copy to one place after the tree is bound (copy_local_files never overwrites), with a regression test for adopt_existing and for the re-claim rebind. Needed lifecycle.py, held by B-wait-wake at the time.
title: [worktree].local_files reaches trees claim binds without W.create: the harness tree adopted via W.current and the item's recorded tree on re-claim (fixes bug B41902e229d)

body: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py flags a version string as a private-network host: shellcheck-py's release tag v0.11.0.1 parses as IPv4 0.11.0.1, which ipaddress calls private (0.0.0.0/8, 'this network'), so pinning that hook fails the suite. 0.0.0.0/8 is never a service's address; only the unspecified 0.0.0.0 itself was excused.

import: a heading that names its phase number ('## Phase 40 — Phase 34 follow-ups') is renamed to its children's id prefix ('34'), colliding with the unrelated, closed Phase 34 (home-simulator import)

import: a sub-heading that says it is live ('### Phase 39 follow-ups (not started)') still inherits its ancestor's SHIPPED STATUS, so its open boxes (38.9, 38.10) are silently dropped as history (home-simulator import)

import: open boxes under a 'Future work' heading inside a SHIPPED section are dropped as history instead of held; the note that reports dropped disposed items gives only a count, so the operator cannot see WHICH open work was dropped (home-simulator: P42.8 items, the Phase 9 5M ramp)

Found importing home-simulator (2026-09-29). (1) '## Phase 40 — Phase 34 follow-ups' with tasks 34.6e.. imported as phase '34': a heading 'Phase N <sep>' keeps N when the child prefix disagrees (P21 under Phase 21 still adopted). (2) '### Phase 39 follow-ups (not started)' under a SHIPPED '## Phase 38' dropped 38.9/38.10: NOT STARTED / IN PROGRESS / REOPENED in a heading is an explicit live verdict. (3) '### P42.8 — Future work' under a SHIPPED section dropped its boxes: FUTURE WORK heading holds. (4) '**38.9 Free-text ...**' (TITLED) ids read; a taken one keeps the old whole-line slug. (5) C11 '(inventory -> todo -> deferred notify)' held: an annotation aside disposes only when a clause leads with the marker; title asides unchanged. (6) closed-skipped note names examples. Measured on run_nemo_run's 1,215 open boxes: only 4.2.1 and 5.2.4 (archived, held) change id; no disposition changes.
title: import: a heading's own phase number and live/future-work status win over ancestors and children; bold 'ID Title' ids are read; only verdict-leading asides dispose; dropped items are named (fixes bugs B-imp-phase-number, B-imp-not-started, B-imp-future-work, B-imp-title-marker)

body: adopt / hooks install run from a LINKED git worktree of ddflow (agent shells here have PYTHONPATH=':' so cwd's code is imported) write that worktree's path into the target project's .mcp.json and git hooks; the worktree is removed on merge, after which the MCP server cannot import and every hook fails closed. Nothing says so.

Found onboarding home-simulator 2026-09-29. Probe: PYTHONPATH=<ddflow linked worktree> ddflow adopt --agents claude in a fresh repo writes PYTHONPATH=<worktree> into .mcp.json and .git/hooks/pre-commit. Redirecting silently to the primary checkout would make ddflow's own tests exercise the wrong code (hooks spawned by tests), so: detect a linked worktree (its .git is a gitdir file) and append a NOTE naming the path and the primary checkout to re-run from. Regression test: package parent in a linked worktree -> adopt output carries the note; fails on current code.
title: adopt and hooks install register the PRIMARY checkout's ddflow (and its venv) when run from a linked worktree, saying so; tests pin the code under test (fixes bug B-adopt-worktree-path)

body: import: '- [ ] **C11** consumable-triggered chains (inventory -> todo -> deferred notify)' is held as DEFERRED: the word describing what the chain does, inside a parenthesised aside after an id-only bold, is read as a verdict; home-simulator's handoff names C11 as the item to start with

ddflow run from an item worktree (python -m ddflow, cwd = worktree) whose branch predates a knob that main's .ddflow/config.toml now sets crashes with a bare ValueError traceback ('unknown knob worktree.local_files', exit 1): config is read from the primary checkout, code from the branch. Seen 2026-09-29 after B-worktree-local-files merged, on B-fix-dup-work-deps. It should say the branch is behind and to merge main (exit 2), not traceback; same class as L-gate-cmd-vs-branch-deps.

Operator 2026-09-29, after the home-simulator cutover: 'the type of work you do, to onboard existing project, as this one, we want to automate - including with the help of the agent, when we connect the MCP/tool for the first time. It shall ask and coordinate the onboarding and cleaning and verification of the workflow via the agent and modify the setup.' Each task below is a step that was done BY HAND for run_nemo_run and home-simulator (see the home-simulator commit 189362d and run_nemo_run e48636ad).
title: Onboarding an existing project is one conversation: attach the MCP, and the agent drives preflight, setup, import, workflow cutover and verification WITH the operator

body: Stages, each with its operator question: 0 preflight (leftover worktrees/branches/stashes: merged -> remove with OK, unmerged -> recover), 1 setup from the PRIMARY checkout with a durable launch path, 2 test gate (detect, measure a baseline in a detached tree, parallelism), 3 import (existing import-existing-project), priorities from a handoff doc, deps for phase-gate tasks, 4 workflow cutover (rulebook sections that write the imported files -> ddflow commands; config from rulebook conventions: forbidden trailers, weekly cadences, sibling repos, live vs journal changelog), 5 freeze the imported files, 6 harness (enabledMcpjsonServers, SessionStart hook, git hooks, machine-local reviewers), 7 verify end to end and commit. Later tasks turn stages into tools; this one makes the whole path exist now.
title: An 'onboard' workflow command (MCP prompt): the one path from 'MCP attached' to a verified cutover, asking the operator at each decision; the handshake of an unadopted or half-cut-over repo points to it
Onboarding preflight: report leftover git/harness worktrees, branches and stashes as merged (--is-ancestor) or holding unique work; remove merged ones only on apply
Onboarding test gate: detect the runner, measure a baseline in a detached clean tree, propose unit_tests (with parallelism, e.g. pytest-xdist) and a live_test smoke

Onboarding cutover: find rulebook lines (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/commands, handoff docs) that tell agents to write the imported files; propose the ddflow replacement per line; generate the freeze ratchet (a pre-commit local hook where the framework is used, else a test)

Onboarding harness: enabledMcpjsonServers for the registered servers, machine-local reviewers.toml/gates.toml copied from a sibling project and git-ignored, a 'ddflow' shell command on the harness PATH when the MCP is PYTHONPATH-pinned
Onboarding imports the agent harness's own per-project memory (Claude Code ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/*.md) as ddflow memory records, deduplicated, with the operator's OK

'ddflow onboard --verify': a live MCP handshake from the REGISTERED entry, hooks armed (and a forbidden-trailer probe refused), brief/next non-empty, freeze ratchet present, frozen files unchanged since import, suite green -- one report

body: init writes .ddflow/.gitignore without reviewers.toml and gates.toml, so a project adopted today commits its machine-local reviewer endpoints (LAN IPs) and machine-sized gate settings on the first 'git add .ddflow' (found by the rubber-duck of B-onboard-command; home-simulator got the lines by hand)

An older ddflow reading the primary's newer .ddflow/config.toml refuses every command: once 1bdefdf added [worktree].local_files to the committed config, running ddflow in any worktree whose code predates it (the tree's own ddflow package is imported from cwd, while config is read from the PRIMARY checkout) fails with ValueError: unknown knob 'worktree.local_files', including the harness trees of live parallel sessions and MCP servers started in them. Repro: cd .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01C1TEJNQxh6UgFfDYxifnmU (code at 5e847a6); ddflow status -> ValueError. Same class as B8ea7a90aea (primary config vs tree code). Fix direction: an unknown knob from a newer config is a warning naming the knob and 'merge main', not a crash; or read config from the tree whose code runs.

Every worktree whose branch predates a knob added on main runs its OWN (older) ddflow code -- the hook's 'python -m' puts the worktree first on sys.path, and harness sessions run from their worktree -- against the primary's NEWER .ddflow/config.toml, and Config.load raises 'unknown knob', so every command and every commit fails for a reason unrelated to the work (hit after B-forbid-trailers' forbidden_trailers; again after 1bdefdf's local_files, which d52d472 then had to disable). (a) Config.load: a key a config FILE carries that this code does not know is kept in cfg.unknown_knobs and skipped, not raised; (b) doctor reports each as a problem-level note ('unknown knob X in .ddflow/config.toml: a typo, or written by a newer ddflow -- merge main'), and config --explain lists them; (c) writers (config --set, --append-toml, workflow gate) stay strict: an unknown key is still refused at write time; (d) env vars unaffected; (e) re-enable local_files = ['.roborev.toml']. Tests: an unknown knob in the file loads with the rest applied and is reported; config --set of an unknown key is still refused.
title: An older ddflow reading a newer config keeps working: an unknown knob in a config FILE is recorded and reported (doctor), not fatal; writes stay strict (fixes bugs Bcfc0d22a09, B9cb7dd1c3b). local_files stays off until no active branch predates this

body: ddflow precommit reports 'git could not list the files' as exit 1 (failure); it is could-not-run, which is exit 2 (found by the rubber_duck reviewer on B-precommit-companion)

ddflow precommit proposes go vet ./... and cargo clippy -D warnings at the pre-commit stage: whole-project checks that re-run on every commit and block every commit of a repo with pre-existing warnings; they belong at pre-push

ddflow precommit proposes hooks whose programs may be absent (docker for hadolint-docker, go/gofmt, cargo, npx) without checking or saying so: a missing one fails every commit, which reads like a refusal

ddflow precommit proposes check-yaml --unsafe for every repository: parse-only mode drops what a full load catches (duplicate keys) everywhere, to accommodate custom tags only some projects (MkDocs) use

schedule.critical_path(state, phase) slices the phase by direct parentage (phase in (i.parent, i.id)), so sub-tasks nested under a task are dropped and the reported wall-clock floor is too short. Probe: P > T > S1, S2 needs S1, S3 needs S2 -> critical_path(st,'P') == ['P'] while critical_path(st) == ['S1','S2','S3']. plan() already switched to state.tasks(phase) for this reason; critical_path is the stale copy (found by roborev duplication analysis, job 845, while on B-fix-dup-work-deps).

gates.toml has two roles that conflict: it is the ONLY supported place to declare human=true gates and pipeline overrides (configwrite.py:289, README), yet this repo git-ignores it as machine-local (D-no-own-services-committed, for worker counts) -- a human checkpoint declared there never reaches another clone. Machine sizing needs its own local layer (found by roborev on B-onboard-command)

complete after merge warns that EVERY gate 'passed on a different tree' even when the tested tree is identical to what landed. completion.verdict takes wt = W.load_path(repo, it.worktree) or repo; merge (remove_on_merge) has already deleted the worktree, so tree_fingerprint runs on the PRIMARY checkout: HEAD is the merge commit (a different commit sha) plus other agents' dirty files. Seen on B-fix-hooks-status-precommit: unit_tests evidence c6fa13645a13+..., merge commit f998381 with 'git diff c6fa136 f998381' empty, yet complete printed the NOTE for unit_tests, standards, critic and rubber_duck. The driver's own order is merge -> complete, so the warning fires on the ordinary path and teaches agents to ignore it. Fix direction: fingerprint the merged branch tip (or compare git tree objects, not commit shas), or check staleness at merge time.

check-commit's staged_paths runs 'git -C <primary> diff --cached' while git hands the hook the WORKTREE's GIT_INDEX_FILE, so it diffs the worktree index against the PRIMARY checkout's HEAD instead of the worktree's: every file master modified since the branch point is reported as staged (demonstrated in a scratch repo: master edits shared.txt, the worktree stages mine.txt, ddflow sees 'A mine.txt, M shared.txt'), and the branch's own already-committed changes too (run_nemo_run DDFLOWPOLICY.1 with nothing staged: '.ddflow/config.toml'). Under commit_without_lease=block a branch behind master is refused for files it never touched; under warn it gets false warnings. Fix: run the staged diff in the tree being committed (_this_worktree), not the resolved primary.

Bug Bba366d9893: staged_paths(repo) runs git -C <primary> diff --cached with the hook's GIT_INDEX_FILE (the worktree's index), comparing it to the primary's HEAD: files master changed since the branch point and the branch's own committed changes read as staged. Fix: every staged-path read in the commit hooks (check_commit, check_views, check_docs and any other staged_paths caller) runs in the tree being committed (_this_worktree / cwd) with that tree's HEAD. Regression test: primary + worktree; master modifies shared.txt after the branch point; the worktree stages only mine.txt under a lease covering mine.txt; with commit_without_lease=block and GIT_INDEX_FILE set as git sets it, check_commit returns 0 and staged_paths is exactly [mine.txt]; fails on current code. Blocks run_nemo_run DDFLOWPOLICY.2 (block).
title: check-commit diffs the index against the committing worktree's HEAD, not the primary's (fixes bug Bba366d9893)

body: complete's stale-gate NOTE ('X passed on a different tree than the one you are completing -- the working tree changed after it ran') fires for gates recorded at the branch's FINAL commit: on B-fix-import-verify-prose, critic and unit_tests carry tree_sha d01121388a64 (= branch HEAD d011213), and complete --sha 90afa8d (the merge commit, whose tree is identical: git diff d011213 90afa8d is empty) still said both ran on a different tree. It appears to compare commit ids, not trees, so every gate is reported stale after ddflow merge -- a warning that is always on is one people learn to ignore, hiding the real stale ones (rubber_duck and standards here really were older).

The evidence contract is vacuous on every surface: api/gates.record adds the MEASURED tree_sha and diff_stat to the evidence dict before G.record checks 'a gate in gates.evidence_required needs evidence to pass', so the dict is never empty and a bare 'gate record <id> <gate> --outcome passed' with no note, command or output is accepted for unit_tests, rubber_duck, critic, standards (and docs). Probe: init, phase add P1, 'ddflow gate record P1 docs --outcome passed' -> exit 0. The check must look at what the CALLER supplied (note/command/output/model), not the measured fields.

Found while adding the docs phase gate (B-docs-phase-gate): api/gates.record sets tree_sha and diff_stat before services.gates.record checks evidence, so 'not evidence' is never true and gates.evidence_required is enforced nowhere through the CLI or MCP. Regression test: a bare passed on an evidence-required gate exits non-zero; with --evidence it passes; the measured fields are still recorded.
title: Evidence-required gates refuse a bare pass again: judge the caller's evidence (note, command, output, model), not the fields ddflow measures itself (fixes the vacuous-evidence bug)

body: A plain 'ddflow import --apply' (no --include-done) keeps a finished phase that open work depends on (plan_import: live_phases |= needs) but imports it EMPTY and OPEN, since its ticked tasks are left out -- so the dependent is never offered. Probe: '## Phase 3' with '- [ ] **3.B** Needs: P5' and '## P5' with two '- [x]' boxes -> import --apply; ddflow next exits 2: '3.B: deps -- phase P5 has no open tasks but is not marked done'. --include-done completes P5 after B-fix-import-done-phases; the plain path should complete such a phase too (evidence: every box under it ticked) or pull its ticked tasks in as done, like _pull_in_needed does for tasks.
bug fixed refuses a shell-command regression test whose text before '::' ends in .py (e.g. 'pytest tests/test_foo.py'): it is taken for a node id, not reported unchecked (critic, deepseek)
bug fixed refuses a real regression test in a non-UTF-8 source file with a coding cookie: _defines reads it as UTF-8 and treats the decode error as missing (critic, deepseek)

ddflow precommit's activation hint names 'the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks' as a fixed string, but the proposal can also install pre-push (go vet / cargo clippy): the hint must name the hook types the config declares (rubber_duck review, DeepSeek; its claim that pre-commit install skips commit-msg is refuted: the config declares default_install_hook_types)
wait: a resource shortfall caused only by the waiter's own lease registers an unsatisfiable wait and burns the whole timeout (critic, _judge_wait resources branch)
wait: an item blocked by a full parallelism cap is refused as hopeless though any release frees a slot; the any-wait treats the same cap as waitable (critic)
wait: under deps_only + report, an any-wait offers an item whose lease expired, which claim then refuses; _claim_blocker omits the expired-lease check (critic)
waits.live_waiters: a registration that is valid JSON but not an object, or has mistyped fields, raises AttributeError/TypeError out of heartbeat/release/merge/complete (critic)
bug fixed refuses a real inherited test: Sub::test_x where test_x is defined on a base class is collected by pytest, but _defines only searches the subclass body (critic, deepseek)
bug fixed accepts a node id pytest never emits: func::nested resolves by descending into a function body instead of only into classes (critic, deepseek)
bug fixed refuses a real test defined under a module-level for/while/match block: _definitions only descends into if/try/with (critic, deepseek)
wait: _waiters catches only OSError; a live registration with a mistyped waiting_on (e.g. an int) raises TypeError out of heartbeat/release/complete (critic, second pass)
bug fixed accepts a node id that names no test: 'tests/test_x.py::' or 'tests/test_x.py::[p]' leaves no name to check and any readable file passes (critic, deepseek)

review split_diff emits a header-only chunk for a file larger than max_chunk_chars: the remainder after the header starts with '\n', re.split yields it as a first piece, current != header, so the header alone is flushed before the first hunk. Reviewers then report 'new file has zero content / no tests' (seen 3x on B-fix-bug-fixed-refuses-unknown with max_chunk_chars=5000). services/review.py:431-441

wait (follow-up, not fixed here): an any-wait whose only blockers need an operator (cycle, expired lease under report) still sleeps to its timeout when an unrelated agent holds any lease, instead of refusing at once; ends in a correct exit 2 (critic pass 3)
waits.live_waiters: a live registration with a non-numeric since raises TypeError in sort/summary, and _waiters then reports NO waiters, hiding the valid ones from the holder (critic pass 3)

Operator 2026-09-29: 'Implement ddflow command to close a bug as invalid / false finding' -- B97355c6d15 (B-wait-wake critic: cap-blocked item refused as hopeless) was shown false by a test, but the only way to close a bug is 'bug fixed', which claims a fix and a regression test that fails on the unfixed code; there is none, so it stays open forever and inflates the open-bug count. Scope: (a) event bug.invalid {reason, evidence}; fold: Bug gains invalid_at/invalid_reason/evidence and a resolution ('fixed'|'invalid'), open = neither; a later bug.found re-merges, never reopens silently; (b) api bug_invalid(id, reason, evidence): refuse (exit 3) an unknown id (same hint as bug_fixed), an already fixed/invalid bug, an empty reason; evidence = a probe command or test node id, resolved statically like bug fixed's --regression-test when it names a test; (c) CLI 'ddflow bug invalid <id> --reason ... [--evidence ...]' + MCP ddflow_bug_invalid, parity-tested; (d) every reader of Bug.open / fixed_at (status open-bug count, brief, recall BUG '[fixed]' label, replay/render reconstruction, progress) shows 'invalid: <reason>' distinctly from fixed -- a false finding is not a fix and must never count toward 'bugs fixed'. Surface wiring (cli.py, mcp.py, api/__init__.py, help.py, test_mcp_parity.py, test_api_layer.py) is held by B-precommit-companion: widen globs once it releases. Regression tests: close-as-invalid on an open bug -> not open, not counted fixed, reason shown; unknown id and fixed bug refused exit 3; empty reason refused. Then close B97355c6d15 with it.
title: ddflow bug invalid: close a recorded bug as a false finding, with a reason and a probe, never as fixed

body: CLI 'ddflow bug fixed <unknown id>' prints 'bug X closed' and exits 0 though api.bug_fixed REFUSED (exit 3) and appended nothing: commands/knowledge.cmd_bug checks only out.exit == FAIL, so the refusal and its hint are swallowed and an agent believes the bug closed (MCP returns 3: CLI/MCP divergence). Probe: init; bug fixed NOPE --regression-test x -> 'bug NOPE closed (regression: x)', exit 0.

ddflow precommit --write writes straight into .pre-commit-config.yaml: a write that fails partway (ENOSPC, EIO) leaves a truncated config that pre-commit then runs, and every later --write refuses because the file exists (rubber_duck review, DeepSeek). Write a temp file and link it into place instead.

The proposed .pre-commit-config.yaml sets no default_stages, so every hook without its own stages (check-merge-conflict, detect-private-key, check-toml, gitleaks...) also runs at commit-msg against the message file and at pre-push: verified with pre-commit run --hook-stage commit-msg; a message with a '=======' line would be refused by check-merge-conflict, and gitleaks runs twice per commit (critic review, DeepSeek).

ddflow precommit --write names its temp file by pid: a temp left by a killed run with the same pid (PID 1 in a container) makes every --write report 'appeared meanwhile; not replaced' (exit 3) while no config exists (rubber_duck review, DeepSeek)

ddflow precommit accepts a --ddflow-cmd with an unbalanced quote (e.g. 'a "b') and proposes/writes local hooks whose entry pre-commit cannot shlex-split, so every commit errors; it only prints 'not found' (bug_hunt, recover-precommit)

ddflow precommit --write returns exists=false with written=true after creating the file, and exists=false alongside 'appeared meanwhile' when it lost a race: the payload contradicts the disk (rubber_duck review, DeepSeek)

ddflow precommit tells the operator to run 'pre-commit install' only on the run that wrote the file with pre-commit already present: written without pre-commit, or re-run after installing it, no output ever says to activate the hooks, so the config runs nothing (critic review, DeepSeek)

schedule.plan reports 'parallelism cap reached (max_parallel_tasks=4); 3 in flight' for ready items ranked past the free slots: with in_flight < cap the cap is NOT reached, one slot is free and offered to a higher-ranked item. An agent waiting for that message to disappear (as told) waits forever while claim of its item succeeds without --force (seen 2026-09-29: B-fix-staged-paths-worktree waited 3h, then claimed fine). The reason should say N slot(s) free, taken by <ids>.

ddflow precommit's activation line says plain 'pre-commit install' installs the hook types of the PROPOSAL; when the file on disk is the operator's own (no default_install_hook_types), that installs only the pre-commit hook and ddflow's check-msg never runs. Name the hook types explicitly: pre-commit install --hook-type ... (rubber_duck review, DeepSeek)

ddflow precommit reads only the root package.json: a monorepo whose eslint/prettier are declared in web/package.json is told 'package.json does not declare it, so there is nothing to run' -- false; the tool exists but a root-level hook could not reach it (roborev review, DeepSeek)

ddflow --json precommit prints {} for a refusal that carries no data (empty or unsplittable --ddflow-cmd): the reason reaches neither stdout nor stderr, while MCP returns it (roborev review, DeepSeek)

ddflow precommit accepts a --ddflow-cmd whose words do not name ddflow (e.g. scripts/run.sh) without saying that 'ddflow hooks status' will then not credit the generated hooks (enforce._runs_check requires 'ddflow' in the command), so the operator is told to install ddflow's hook again (roborev design review, DeepSeek)

ddflow_precommit over MCP turns an empty ddflow_cmd into 'ddflow' (a.get(...) or 'ddflow') while the CLI and API refuse it with exit 3: the same input succeeds on one surface and is refused on the other (roborev design review, DeepSeek)

ddflow precommit's activation line always passes explicit --hook-type flags from the PROPOSAL; pre-commit then installs only those, so an operator's own config declaring more (e.g. pre-push in default_install_hook_types) is under-installed. Plain 'pre-commit install' honours a config that declares its types; flags are needed only when the file on disk declares none (roborev design review, DeepSeek; introduced by the Bd6e6d40f1e fix)
ddflow precommit --write refused over an existing file says 'compare it with the proposal' but prints no proposal and does not say how to see one (roborev design review, DeepSeek)
ddflow precommit's missing-program note says each would 'fail every commit', but go/cargo clippy run only at pre-push (roborev review, DeepSeek)

ddflow --json precommit prints nothing on stdout when the operation fails (exit 1, e.g. the write fails): the FAIL early return precedes the JSON branch, so a JSON consumer gets no body while other outcomes get one (critic review, DeepSeek)

Flaky: tests/test_jobs.py::test_a_job_is_launched_detached_watched_and_its_exit_code_collected failed once under load (unit_tests gate on B-precommit-companion, tree 6b8018c, while LAN reviews ran): 'job end' on a job just launched returned 0, 'a running job was recorded as ended'; the rerun on the same tree passed (2365 passed). Timing-dependent: the job likely exited before 'job end' ran.

The pre-commit companion note promises that ddflow precommit prints a 'pre-commit install --hook-type ...' line; for the generated config it prints plain 'pre-commit install' (roborev review, DeepSeek)

ddflow precommit --write: an OSError other than FileNotFoundError from removing the temp file (finally: tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)) escapes as a traceback after the config was linked into place, outside the 0/1/2/3 exit vocabulary (roborev review, DeepSeek)

A dict[str, str] config knob set from the environment as JSON str()-casts every value: DDFLOW_AGENT_FAMILIES='{"core": null}' loads as {'core': 'None'} instead of being refused (config._coerce_dict, pre-existing; raised by the DeepSeek rubber-duck on B-fix-trailer-names-item, not fixed there)

The LAN DeepSeek reviewer truncates one chunk of a ~42k-char diff in most rounds (64000 of 64000 tokens spent reasoning, no answer), so ddflow review records rubber_duck/critic PARTIAL; seen 4 times on B-fix-trailer-names-item. [[reviewer]].max_tokens or max_chunk_chars needs tuning (machine-local config)

complete warns 'unit_tests passed on a different tree' when it did not: stale_evidence fingerprints the item's worktree, which merge has already removed, so it falls back to / fails on a path that is gone and compares against another HEAD. Seen on B-fix-trailer-names-item: unit_tests ran on 9720374, whose tree is byte-identical to the merged 5de4bb6 (git diff empty), yet complete warned (services/completion.py stale_evidence after merge)

Bug B9cb7dd1c3b: a worktree nested under the primary (.claude/worktrees/*, .kilo/worktrees/*) imports ITS OWN ddflow code but reads the PRIMARY's .ddflow/config.toml; config.py:1186 raises ValueError('unknown knob ...') on any knob newer than the tree's code, so every command fails there (12 harness trees broken by enforce.forbidden_trailers; local_files would have broken 3 more -> disabled in d52d472). Operator 2026-09-30 agreed: keep local_files off until this is fixed, then turn it back on. Research first: why that code/config pairing (cwd import vs config discovery), and whether the right fix is (a) an unknown knob in a known section is a warning naming the knob and 'your ddflow is older than this config: merge main' (a typo'd knob must still be caught -- e.g. refuse when the SAME code's own templates/docs do not know it, or keep refusing in the primary/--strict), and/or (b) reading config from the tree whose code runs. Mind decision/lesson on silent-knob-drop: never silently ignore. Sibling: B-fix-gate-config-drift (bug B8ea7a90aea, services/gates.py) is the same primary-config-vs-tree-code class for gate commands -- do not take its scope. Regression test: config with a knob the code does not know -> commands still run and name the knob (fails on current code with ValueError); a typo'd knob is still reported. Last step: uncomment local_files = ['.roborev.toml'] in .ddflow/config.toml (d52d472's note) and verify an older nested harness tree (e.g. .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01PsvUbFf1s1M5qBj52UYuhg) still runs 'ddflow status'.
title: An older ddflow reading a newer .ddflow/config.toml warns on an unknown knob instead of refusing every command; then re-enable [worktree].local_files (fixes bug B9cb7dd1c3b)

body: import --verify / import notes flag home-simulator phase 36.5 'Orchestration recipes beyond the shipped two' as 'says the work is finished while a task is open': _DONE_MARKER matches the word 'shipped' in heading prose, not only a status (SHIPPED, ✅, (done)); a permanent false alarm on an onboarded project

ddflow review sends git's hunk-header funcname context, which misleads reviewers: for a TOML diff it is the PREVIOUS block's last line ('@@ -104,11 +106,12 @@ default = true' above the memory companion's hunk in companions.toml). On B-fix-companions-stale the LAN DeepSeek critic (rounds 2 and 3) and rubber_duck (round 3) each reported 'memory is still default = true' although memory is default = false; the 'default = true' they cited is context7's, taken from the hunk header. Candidate fix: build review diffs with a funcname that cannot mislead (e.g. -c diff.default.xfuncname='^$' or strip hunk-header context), or say in the reviewer prompt that text after @@ is not part of the hunk.

the research gate's instruction (services/gates.py:140) and run_nemo_run's CLAUDE.md tell agents to run 'ddflow research add --verdict ...', but the CLI command is 'ddflow research --question ... --verdict ...' ('add' -> 'unrecognized arguments'); every agent following the gate text gets an error (found onboarding home-simulator)

config_paths already reads .ddflow/local/{config,gates,reviewers}.toml last (git-ignored via local/). This repo instead ignored .ddflow/gates.toml and .ddflow/reviewers.toml in the root .gitignore, so human=true gates declared in gates.toml (the only supported place) never reach another clone. Fix: root .gitignore stops ignoring .ddflow/gates.toml; machine sizing moves to .ddflow/local/gates.toml, reviewers to .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml; init's .ddflow/.gitignore ignores a top-level reviewers.toml and says where machine values go; the onboard prompt points there. Regression: git check-ignore .ddflow/gates.toml is false in this repo; init's .gitignore ignores reviewers.toml and not gates.toml.

Fixed in 7536d99 (scripts/ci/build-probe.sh probes from a scratch dir and refuses if ddflow is not from site-packages; the stripped wheel now exits 1). Open until a pytest regression test pins it.

companions: an entry under a companion's id counts as 'registered' whatever it holds -- {} , "x", 5, [] (pre-existing on main: get_server(...) is not None). Status.usable is then True and gate_coverage counts the gate as covered while nothing can launch; register() meanwhile would write (its == want check fails), so reader and writer disagree. Found by roborev on 5cd42dc (B-fix-companions-stale, which fixed only the null case). Fix: count an id entry only when _launch_of(entry) is not None or it has a url.

Operator 2026-09-30, first: always bump the minor version on publish; trigger = every push to main that changes shipped code (ddflow/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile, docker-entrypoint.sh, .dockerignore); docs/tests/event-log-only pushes publish nothing; CI runs scripts/bump.sh and commits 'release X.Y.Z' to main before publishing, then tags vX.Y.Z once everything published. body: scripts/bump.sh's re-read check imports ddflow from the tree, and Python trusts __pycache__ when source size and whole-second mtime match: two bumps within one second with same-length versions (0.1.2 -> 0.1.3) read the previous bytecode and fail 'bump did not take: SERVER_INFO is 0.1.2' although every file was written. Reproduced: 3 quick patch bumps, the 3rd fails; with __pycache__ removed between them all pass.

The pre-push hooks fail with 'files were modified by this hook' although every test passed: pre-commit diffs the WHOLE working tree before/after each hook, and in the primary checkout ddflow agents append to tracked .ddflow/events/*.jsonl continuously, so any hook that runs long enough (the test suites) races them. Seen on the operator's push 2026-09-30: fix-shipped, fix-local, fix-launch logs modified during the run.

title: Pre-push checks run in a scratch worktree of the pushed commit (agents' event-log writes no longer fail them) and the test suites run as one parallel pytest session (fixes the pre-push race bug)

body: claim refuses a worktree still 'bound' to an item that is merged and released: B-release-every-push was merged (tree 0 ahead of main), released with ddflow release, and open only for a deferred review, yet ddflow claim B-prepush-isolated in the same (adopted) tree refuses 'already bound to B-release-every-push, which is still open'. A tree holding nothing unmerged cannot lose work to a second item; release should unbind it, or the check should ask whether the tree is ahead of base.

title: doctor warns when an untracked .ddflow/gates.toml or .ddflow/reviewers.toml sits beside .ddflow/local/ (machine values under the pre-B-fix-local-layer convention, one git add away from being committed)

body: 'ddflow reviewers detect --write' (api/review.py:133) and 'reviewers add --base-url' append [[reviewer]] blocks with endpoints to the COMMITTED .ddflow/config.toml; decision D-no-own-services-local-dir puts them in .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml (found by the rubber-duck of B-fix-local-layer)

ddflow review on an item claimed --no-worktree reviews the PRIMARY checkout's working tree (other agents' uncommitted event-log appends, 43 KB) instead of the item's commits, and records the gate PASSED: B-prepush-isolated.rubber_duck = passed with 0 findings on a diff containing none of the change. A review of the wrong diff must refuse (or say what it reviewed and record unavailable), never pass.

heartbeat revives an EXPIRED lease with its claim-time globs: update --globs on an item whose lease has lapsed changes item.globs only (plan_retarget leaves an expired lease for recovery), and the later heartbeat renews the lease without them, so the commit hook reports the paths just added as not covered. Reproduced: claim T5 i/* (ttl 2 s, grace 1 s), wait, update --globs i/*,j/*, heartbeat -> lease globs [i/*]; check-commit: j/f not covered. Seen live on B-prepush-isolated (demos/, pyproject.toml).

title: merge lands a branch for an item claimed without a worktree (--branch, else the caller's branch); review never diffs the primary's working tree for an item; claim may reuse a tree whose bound item is merged and released; heartbeat reviving a lapsed lease takes the item's current globs (fixes B0ff09a29a5, B60de9a57ed and the heartbeat-globs bug)
Regression test for the CI build probe: a wheel missing its templates or with a broken console script fails it (closes Ba5345f975d)

body: gate run of a command gate for an item claimed --no-worktree runs in the PRIMARY checkout and records the result as the item's: B-no-worktree-lifecycle.unit_tests = passed with diff_stat files=0 -- main's suite, not the change (so was B-prepush-isolated's). A command gate must run where the item's work is -- its tree, else the tree of the branch it is worked on -- or record unavailable.

body: Operator 2026-09-30, from research Rfa535c6747: review time is the reviewer's reasoning length (random per call, 6k-42k tokens for the same diff, a runaway tail that truncates at max_tokens) times chunks sent one after another, while the LAN server sits idle (8 concurrent: each 28% slower, 5.7x throughput). (1) chunks in parallel, capped by [[reviewer]].max_concurrency; (2) [[reviewer]].hedge copies per chunk, the first on-contract answer wins and the rest are CANCELLED (connection closed / process killed), so neither the server nor the CLI waits on them. Defaults for every project: hedge=2, max_concurrency=4; this project's LAN reviewer tuned in its machine-local config.
title: Reviews send chunks in parallel and race hedged copies of each (first valid answer wins, losers cancelled); on by default for every project

body: An older ddflow refuses a [[reviewer]] block carrying a newer field instead of warning and skipping it: adding hedge/max_concurrency to .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml made the installed ddflow fail every review command ('ValueError: unknown field(s) [hedge, max_concurrency] in [[reviewer]] #1'). The config.toml forward-compat fix (B9cb7dd1c3b) did not cover reviewer blocks, so every new reviewer knob breaks mixed-version clones sharing a config.

init's .gitattributes/.gitignore appends are skipped on a SUBSTRING match: an existing '.ddflow/events/*.jsonl -diff' line suppresses the merge=union line, and '.ddflow-worktrees-old/' suppresses the .ddflow-worktrees/ ignore (found by rubber_duck review of B-fix-mcp-setup-init)

gate_config_drift classifies from working trees: an uncommitted gate edit in the primary on top of a committed gate change hides the 'behind' drift (bare test failure again), and an uncommitted gate edit in the item tree mislabels a behind branch as 'own'. Found by critic review of B-fix-gate-config-drift. Fix: classify on committed specs (tree HEAD vs fork vs primary HEAD).

review.split_diff: a single file bigger than the chunk budget yields a HEADER-ONLY chunk (the newline after the header counts as a 'hunk', so the first real hunk overflows and flushes the bare header) and the next chunk glues the hunk header onto the '+++ b/<file>' line ('+++ b/t.py@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@'). The reviewer then reports the new file as EMPTY: both DeepSeek reviews of B-fix-gate-config-drift raised HIGH/MEDIUM 'tests/test_gate_config_drift.py is an empty file' findings and recorded rubber_duck/critic failed. Probe: split_diff('diff --git a/t.py b/t.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/t.py
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
' + 50 lines, 400) -> first piece is the 71-char header alone. Root: header = f.split('
@@',1)[0] drops the '
' into the hunk list.

cleanup apply's per-removal re-check (fresh fold) and the removal are not atomic: a claim appended between the re-read and 'git worktree remove' still loses its tree. The re-check must run under the event log's append lock (EventLog.transaction), held across the removal, so a claim either lands first and is seen or lands after and recreates the tree. Found by rubber_duck review (deepseek).

review.split_diff emits a HEADER-ONLY chunk (diff --git ... +++ b/<file>, no @@ hunk) when a file's first hunk would overflow max_chunk_chars: the header plus the lone newline before '@@' is flushed as its own piece. The reviewer then reports the file as empty. Reproduced: a new 151-line test file at max_chunk_chars=5000 splits into a 175-char header-only chunk + the 6430-char hunk; rubber_duck on B-fix-mcp-setup-init flagged tests/test_setup_writes_init.py as 'zero bytes'. Fix: do not count the pre-hunk remainder as content (compare current.strip() to header.strip()) before flushing.

gate_config_drift compares committed layers only, but load_gates also merges the git-ignored .ddflow/local layer: when the local layer overrides a run field (e.g. command) the command that RAN is the local one, yet a committed change on main vs an older branch was reported as 'behind' and a genuine failure recorded unavailable. Found by rubber_duck review. Fix: overlay the primary's local layer on every spec compared.

gate_config_drift checks 'own' before 'behind': a branch that committed any run-field edit (e.g. timeout_s) and is ALSO behind a committed command change on main is labelled 'own' and recorded as a bare test FAILURE of main's command -- the original B8ea7a90aea symptom. Found by rubber_duck review. Fix: a base change since the fork is 'behind' first.

tests/test_review_parallel.py::test_a_command_reviewers_losing_copy_is_killed is racy: the losing copy writes its pid with 'echo $$ > pid' (truncate, then write) after mkdir, and the winning copy answers at once, so the review can return and cancel the loser between the truncate and the write; the test then reads '' -> ValueError. Seen 2026-10-01 in the pre-push hook (1 failed, 2642 passed). The product behaviour held (REVIEWED, in time).

Write the pid atomically (tmp + mv) and make the winning copy answer only once the pid file exists, so the review cannot return before the loser's pid is on disk. Test-only change. Blocks the operator's git push (pre-push runs the suite).
title: The hedged-reviewer kill test cannot race its own pid file (fixes bug B-flaky-hedge-pidfile)

body: Operator 2026-10-01 asked whether ddflow can work with GitHub Copilot CLI's Project HydraFusion (research R7dbec5e53a, https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/project-hydrafusion-frontier-quality-via-multi-model-orchestration/). It can drive it through the existing copilot target, but: family_for('hydrafusion') == '' so complete refuses ('author's model is not in [agent].families'), and HydraFusion picks models across providers per task (single / cascade / critique), so no single author family exists; its internal different-family critique is invisible to ddflow and is not gate evidence. Scope: (a) [agent].routers (or a families value that is a list): a model name that maps to a SET of families, shipped default hydrafusion -> an EMPTY set: research R-hydrafusion-families (CONFIRMED) found GitHub publishes no fixed roster, so a guessed set could wrongly pass a reviewer as independent; the operator lists the families per plan. Chosen shape: a new knob [agent].routers (dict[str, list[str]]), not list values in [agent].families; (b) reviewer_independence: an author that is a set is independent of a reviewer only if the reviewer's family is outside the WHOLE set; a router author with an unknown member set is never assumed independent -- the refusal names the knob to set; (c) once the set is configured, complete/merge --model hydrafusion works with this repo's DeepSeek reviewer iff deepseek is outside the set; (d) github-copilot delta: HydraFusion is strongest on first-turn single-prompt tasks (per the post), so drive it per step -- claim, then one HydraFusion turn for implement, then ddflow gates -- not the whole loop in one conversation; its internal critique does not replace rubber_duck/critic. Regression tests: hydrafusion author + deepseek reviewer -> independent; + a reviewer in the set -> refused naming the overlap; an unconfigured router -> refused with the knob named; a plain single-family author unchanged. Fails on current code.
title: A router author (Copilot HydraFusion) is a SET of families: independence needs a reviewer outside all of them; the Copilot delta says to drive it per step

body: router_set returns the FIRST matching [agent].routers needle, so overlapping needles (hydra + hydrafusion, or hydrafusion + hydrafusion-pro) give an under-approximated or wrong set depending on key order, and a reviewer from an omitted family passes reviewer_independence as independent (false pass). Found by the rubber_duck and critic re-review.

publish #36: mcp-registry rejects ddflow-mcp: 'PyPI package ownership validation failed. The server name io.github.delian/ddflow-mcp must appear as mcp-name: io.github.delian/ddflow-mcp in the package README'. README.md (the PyPI long description) lacks it, and the Dockerfile lacks the io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name label the registry checks for the two OCI packages. README.md is also not in the publish workflow's path filter, so a README-only fix would not release.

title: MCP registry ownership: README carries mcp-name, the image carries io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name, the publish workflow refuses to upload a release the registry would reject, and a README change releases (fixes bug B-mcp-registry-ownership)

body: Under [enforce].commit_without_lease=block with the pre-commit framework, 'ddflow merge' (its merge commit in the PRIMARY checkout) is refused with 'You hold: (no live lease)' whenever the lease's events are not yet committed: pre-commit stashes unstaged files before running hooks, which reverts the primary's uncommitted .ddflow/events/<agent>.jsonl, so check-commit folds a log without the lease (and its heartbeats). Reproduced in run_nemo_run ONBOARDFIX.1 2026-10-01: refused twice with a live lease (1799 s left); the same check run outside git passed; committing the event log first, then 'ddflow merge', succeeded. ddflow merge also leaves the primary mid-merge (MERGE_HEAD) on that refusal. Fix options: read leases from a source pre-commit cannot stash (git-ignored lease file / index.db), or have merge commit the event log before the merge commit.

ddflow_claim with as_agent (a subagent sharing its parent's MCP connection) adopts the CONNECTION's harness worktree via adopt_existing, binding the subagent's item to the parent session's tree and branch: B-local-config-surfaces (agent local-config-surfaces) is bound to the parent's .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_015Nbh... on worktree-bridge-cse_015Nbh..., and the next subagent's ddflow_claim (contest-gaps, B-fix-contest-gaps) is refused 'this worktree is already bound to B-local-config-surfaces'. A claim under an as_agent identity different from the connection's should create its own tree (as the CLI from the primary does), not adopt the caller's. Workaround used: ddflow --agent contest-gaps claim from the primary checkout.

ddflow_claim with as_agent (a subagent sharing its parent's MCP connection) adopts the CONNECTION's linked worktree (worktree.adopt_existing) instead of creating the item's own tree: the first sibling binds the parent session's tree to its item, and every other sibling's MCP claim is then refused 'this worktree is already bound to <other item>'. Observed: B-local-config-surfaces (agent local-config-surfaces) adopted .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_015NbhRCT5XtidHYRvkjBCLK; B-fix-adopt-launcher's MCP claim was refused; the CLI claim run from the primary tree worked. A claim made as a named subagent should not adopt the shared connection's tree.

Lease contest OVER-report (safe direction, pre-existing): when a late renewal proves a displaced claim was live at its takeover, _late_renewal also joins the lease displayed at that moment into the contest whether or not it overlapped anyone (test_divergence _three_hops: carol [6000,7800] is contested though only alice/bob overlapped). The displayed lease stays in the contest after it is itself displaced. Kept deliberately in B-fix-contest-gaps because removing it makes `resolve --keep <current holder>` impossible: resolve refuses a keep that is the displayed lease but not a contestant. Fix both together (needs ddflow/api/items.py): let resolve keep the displayed lease, then join only pairwise overlaps.

'ddflow reviewers add --preset ollama' (any preset with a launch table, without --no-launch) writes launch = {"command": ..., "ready_url": ...} via json.dumps -- JSON, not a TOML inline table -- so the config file it appends to no longer parses and every later command reading reviewers fails

Pre-existing on main (b6a424a), found triaging the DeepSeek critic on B-fix-contest-gaps: a late renewal of a TTL-displaced claim joins its displacer `by` unconditionally, even after `by` was released. Fold h1 0+10, h2 15+10 (displaces h1), release h2 by event, then h1 renewal at 8 -> lease_contest [h1, h2] naming the RELEASED claim, with no displayed lease; the same events with the renewal folded before the release give no contest. Fold-order dependent, and violates the overjoin invariants (no released claim anywhere; a standing contest displays a claim).

next --phase <id> silently returns 'Nothing actionable (0 ready, 0 running, 0 blocked)' when <id> is not an item at all (e.g. '159', whose tasks live under 159.A..159.I). Expected: an 'unknown phase' error (exit 1/2 with a message), or prefix-matching child phases. Repro on run_nemo_run: 'ddflow next --phase 159' -> empty, while 'ddflow show 159' -> 'no such item'. A driver reading the empty set as 'phase done' stops early (seen by the implement loop, 2026-10-01).

MCP ddflow_status has no size bound: on run_nemo_run (4831 tasks) it returns 721,813 chars / 18,351 lines (completed_tasks lists every done task), which exceeds the harness's tool-output limit and is spilled to a file. Brief has session.brief_max_tokens; status needs the same (summary counts + in-flight + ready by default, full lists behind a flag).

status/brief undercount the queue: items held back ONLY by schedule.max_parallel_tasks are counted as neither ready nor blocked, so tasks.total != done+running+ready+blocked. REPRO (home-simulator repo, 2026-10-01, schedule.max_parallel_tasks=4): before any claim, ddflow status -> tasks {total:45, done:0, running:0, ready:4, blocked:22} (19 dep-free items vanish: C6, 36.5a, 37.1a-e, 37.6a, 38.9, 38.10...). After claiming 4 items: ddflow --json status -> {total:45, done:0, running:4, ready:0, blocked:22} (sum 26), while ddflow --json next lists 41 blocked, those 19 with reason='state', detail='parallelism cap reached (schedule.max_parallel_tasks=4)'. So next and status disagree on the same snapshot. Effect: operator reading status/brief ('Ready now: 4') concludes only 4 items are startable and cannot see the other dep-free ones; brief prints 'These 4 are independent' implying the rest are not. EXPECTED: one classification shared by next/status/brief/board: report cap-held items explicitly (e.g. tasks.held_by_cap or ready_capped, or count them as ready with a 'cap reached' note), and keep the invariant total == sum of buckets (add a test asserting it). Secondary: human 'ddflow next' output lists dependency-blocked items first and buries the cap reason; when the cap is the only reason, say 'N more items are ready but held by max_parallel_tasks=K' in the summary line.

Follow-up of B-local-config-surfaces, which could not touch ddflow/services/adopt.py (held by B-fix-adopt-launcher). The commented [[reviewer]] example in adopt.py's config template should point at .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml (reviewers add / detect --write default there, --shared commits), and one short comment block should say what is committed (generic project policy) vs local (your endpoints, hosts, key variable names, machine sizing: ddflow config --local). Test: a fresh init's config.toml mentions .ddflow/local and no longer claims detect --write fills in that file.
title: init's config.toml template says reviewers detect --write 'fills this in'; it now writes .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml -- say so, and say services go in the git-ignored local layer

body: A subagent sharing its parent's MCP connection passes as_agent; the server's called_from is the PARENT's harness worktree, so claim adopted it (adopt_existing) and bound the subagent's item to the parent's tree and branch; the next subagent was then refused 'this worktree is already bound to ...'. Fix in the MCP dispatcher: the connection's location belongs to the connection's identity; a claim under a different per-call identity is not standing there, so it does not adopt (it creates its own tree, as the CLI from the primary does). An as_agent equal to the connection's own identity (declared or derived) still adopts. Items already bound keep their recorded tree (rebound path), so live bindings are untouched.
title: ddflow_claim under an as_agent other than the connection's identity creates its own tree instead of adopting the connection's harness worktree (fixes bug B7c7a0d9222)

body: B-late-renewal-overjoin: _late_renewal joins the lease displayed at that moment into the contest whether or not it overlapped anyone (test_divergence _three_hops: carol [6000,7800] contested though only alice/bob overlapped). Kept in B-fix-contest-gaps because resolve refuses a keep that is the displayed lease but not a contestant. Probe on main (bbbe066): three_hops keep carol exits 0, releases nothing, and leaves alice/bob contested -- so the over-join never actually let the current holder win; and a plain double claim followed by a clean TTL takeover (alice 1000, bob 1500, carol 9000) refuses --keep carol outright. Fix: resolve accepts the displayed lease, and when it met none of the contest releases every contestant (each ended before it took the item); then _late_renewal joins only pairwise overlaps. Property tests: exact contest with renewals.
title: A late renewal joins only the claims it overlapped; resolve can keep the current holder when it met none of the contest (fixes bug B-late-renewal-overjoin)

body: resolve cannot settle a contest in favour of the current holder when that holder met none of the contestants (pre-existing on main bbbe066, independent of any late renewal). Plain double claim then clean TTL takeover: alice 1000+1800, bob 1500+1800, carol 9000+1800 -> contest [alice,bob], carol displayed; 'resolve T --keep carol' exits 1 'names none of T's contestants'. With the late-renewal over-join (test_divergence _three_hops) carol IS a contestant, and 'resolve --keep carol' exits 0, releases nothing, and leaves alice/bob contested -- a success that settled nothing. So the over-join B-late-renewal-overjoin kept for this never made it work. Only ways out today hand the item back to a lapsed claim and release the live holder.

A lease expires silently while its holder waits on ddflow's OWN long commands: 'ddflow review <id>' (22-25 min on a LAN reasoning model) and 'ddflow gate run <id> unit_tests' (13 min) do not renew the lease of <id>, so the agent's next commit is refused by the commit_without_lease hook ('You hold: (no live lease)'). Seen on run_nemo_run 159.A.8, 2026-10-01. Expected: review / gate run / tests --item heartbeat the item they run for (they already know its id), or the refusal says the lease EXPIRED and that 'ddflow heartbeat <id>' renews it.

The commit hook warns 'no live lease' for a commit made by a subagent that holds a live lease under a per-call as_agent identity (seen by local-config-surfaces on B-local-config-surfaces): the hook resolves the identity from the tree/connection, not the agent that actually holds the lease, so a correct commit is warned against.

ddflow_merge returns the merged branch's head as its sha (4dd7b3e for B-local-config-surfaces) instead of the merge commit on main (cb36953); a caller recording or reporting the merge cites the wrong commit.

claim/update --globs: repeated flag silently keeps only the LAST value, and a JSON-array string is split on commas into literal junk globs. Source: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:390 cl.add_argument('--globs') (plain store; same for task add :314). REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10f claim 34.10f --globs a --globs docs/CHANGELOG.md --globs docs/RESEARCH.md --globs README.md ... --globs configs/default.toml' -> exit 0, lease.acquired event globs=['configs/default.toml'] only. The overlap check therefore never saw CHANGELOG/RESEARCH/README, and a sibling (34.8g) leased the same files; the conflict surfaced only later at 'update' and as a commit-hook warning. Second repro: impl-34.8g passed --globs '["home_simulator/world/speaker.py", "..."]' -> lease globs recorded as '["home_simulator/world/speaker.py"', '"home_simulator/config/speaker.py"', ... (brackets and quotes kept, nothing matches). EXPECTED: action='append' + comma split (or reject a repeated flag with exit 3), and validate each glob (reject [ ] " , warn when a glob matches no tracked file and no new path). Regression test: repeated --globs yields union; JSON-ish input rejected.

update --globs REPLACES the lease's globs instead of adding, with no warning, so an agent widening scope (the driver says 'ddflow update <ID> --globs ...' FIRST when you need to write outside globs) silently drops its earlier paths from conflict detection. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.10f): after claim, 'ddflow update 34.10f --globs "<5 paths>"' -> task.updated globs = exactly those 5; commit hook then listed only the 5. EXPECTED: either --add-globs/--globs+ semantics, or the driver/help text must say update replaces and show the before/after diff of globs on stdout. Also: 'ddflow show <id>' does not print the item's globs or the current lease globs, so the operator cannot see what a lease covers without reading the event log - add 'globs:' and 'lease: holder/worktree/globs' lines to show.

Lease records the WRONG worktree when a subagent claims via the parent's shared MCP connection with as_agent. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): parent session in .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE (MCP server cwd) spawned subagents with Claude Code Agent isolation=worktree; subagent impl-34.8g called ddflow_claim(as_agent=impl-34.8g) while working in .claude/worktrees/agent-a92981182770b640f. Its lease.renewed event recorded branch=worktree-bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE worktree=.claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE (the PARENT's tree), while siblings that claimed from the shell got their own tree correctly. Consequence: ddflow merge/review for 34.8g target the parent's (empty) branch, i.e. silently merge nothing or review the wrong diff, and two identities share one worktree. EXPECTED: the MCP claim must take an explicit worktree/cwd parameter (or refuse 'adopt' when as_agent differs from the connection identity and the worktree is already the connection's), and merge must refuse when the leased branch has no commits ahead of main while the item has an implement gate passed. Test: as_agent claim from a shared connection never adopts the connection's worktree.

ddflow review: same PARTIAL outcome exits with different codes by gate. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.10f, reviewer lan-<served-model>): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10f review 34.10f --gate rubber_duck' printed 'PARTIAL ... 5/6 chunk(s) reviewed' + 'recorded 34.10f.rubber_duck = partial' and exited 0; 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10f review 34.10f --gate critic --intent ...' printed 'PARTIAL ... 5/7 chunk(s)' + 'recorded ... = partial' and exited 3. EXPECTED: one exit code for partial regardless of gate (not 0, since 0 reads as a clean pass to scripts; 1 or a documented code). Related: in both runs chunk 4 hit the reviewer's 64k reasoning-token cap with no verdict; with default [[reviewer]].max_tokens/max_chunk_chars any diff > ~40k chars loses coverage. Suggest auto-split+retry of a truncated chunk at half size before reporting partial, and name the files in the unreviewed chunk in the output so the author knows what lacks coverage.

bug fixed --regression-test accepts only one test; given several (e.g. ';'-separated) it reports the test 'exists in no worktree', which misdiagnoses the input instead of saying only one test is accepted or accepting a list (seen by fix-renewal-overjoin closing B-late-renewal-overjoin).

Left open by B-fix-asagent-claim: (1) the other MCP tools (gate_run, review, merge, precommit, tests) still resolve a subagent's as_agent call to the parent's harness worktree, which matters for an item claimed with --no-worktree; (2) 'ddflow --agent X claim' run from inside a harness worktree still adopts that tree, since the CLI has no connection identity to compare against, so the workaround is to claim from the primary checkout.

Follow-up to B5c32cbb5c1: a wrong worktree binding on an item is STICKY and blocks the correct merge. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.8g): after the MCP claim bound .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE, the owner ran from its real tree (.claude/worktrees/agent-a92981182770b640f): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g release 34.8g' then 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g claim 34.8g --globs ...' -> 'the item's own tree, from an earlier claim ... cd .../bridge-cse... and work there'; with --no-worktree the bridge tree still shows in 'ddflow show 34.8g'. Then 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g merge 34.8g --branch worktree-agent-a92981182770b640f --keep' refused: 'has its own worktree on worktree-bridge-cse_...; it lands that branch ... Drop --branch'. Without --branch it would merge the bound branch, which had ZERO commits ahead of main, and record the item merged. Operator workaround: fast-forwarded the bridge branch to the real branch, then merge -> d7fbf00. EXPECTED: (a) release/re-claim (or 'ddflow update <id> --worktree PATH') can rebind; (b) merge refuses (exit 3) when the bound branch has no commits ahead of base, instead of 'merging' nothing; (c) --branch allowed with an explicit --rebind. Also: 'complete' then printed 'standards/unit_tests passed on a different tree than the one you are completing' although the content was identical (0803640) - the tree fingerprint is taken from the bound (wrong) worktree, producing a false warning.

Commit hook resolves identity from the worktree, not from the lease holder/--agent, so it blames the owner for its own lease.
