REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): impl-34.8g held the lease on 34.8g; 'git commit' in its own worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a92981182770b640f printed 'paths ... leased by ANOTHER agent ... held by 34.8g (impl-34.8g) ... You hold: (no live lease)'. Every commit from a subagent worktree with an as_agent identity gets this false warning, which trains agents to ignore the real cross-agent warning. EXPECTED: hook honours DDFLOW_AGENT env / a per-worktree identity file written at claim time, and matches by lease holder; test: owner committing in its own tree gets no warning.

Global --agent flag only works BEFORE the subcommand. REPRO: 'ddflow brief --agent impl-34.8g --item 34.8g' -> 'unrecognized arguments: --agent' (exit 2); 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g brief --item 34.8g' works. Agents naturally append flags, and the drivers/prompts tell subagents to 'pass --agent on every call' without saying where. EXPECTED: accept --agent (and other global options like --json, --repo) after the subcommand too (argparse parents= on each subparser), or document the position in every driver; test both positions.

LAN DeepSeek reviewer defaults make 'ddflow review' practically unusable: reasoning consumes the whole [[reviewer]].max_tokens (64k) budget before any verdict. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, reviewer lan-<served-model>, <served-model>): item 34.8g review of fe9e740: chunk 7/9 truncated in BOTH rubber_duck and critic; re-review of a 12K-char diff (72de30c): all 3 chunks truncated -> unavailable; each run took 27-44 minutes. Item 34.10f: chunk 4 truncated in both gates. EXPECTED: detect 'finish_reason=length with no content' and retry that chunk with a reasoning-effort cap (e.g. reasoning_effort/thinking budget param) or a smaller chunk, before declaring partial; ship a sane default max_tokens/max_chunk_chars for reasoning models; report the per-chunk file list for what went unreviewed; consider a wall-clock budget so a review cannot take 40 min silently.

Additional evidence for Bdc85898c40 (claim --globs): with TEN repeated --globs flags the claim recorded NO globs at all. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8f claim 34.8f --globs a.py --globs b.py ... (10 flags)' -> 'claimed 34.8f', exit 0; 'ddflow --json show 34.8f' -> item globs [] AND lease globs []. (For 34.10f the same pattern kept only the last value, so the outcome differs by path - possibly the last value was a path the claim filtered.) Either way the agent ran with zero conflict coverage while believing it had declared 10 paths; a single comma-separated --globs on 'update' worked. EXPECTED: never accept a claim whose parsed globs differ from what was passed without saying so; print the recorded globs on every claim.

MCP ddflow_claim judges the MCP SERVER's cwd worktree, so the 2nd subagent sharing a connection is refused. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): parent session's MCP server cwd = .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE; subagent impl-34.8g's MCP claim had bound that tree (B5c32cbb5c1). Subagent impl-34.8f (own tree .claude/worktrees/agent-abfc3812795993a23) called ddflow_claim(as_agent='impl-34.8f', id='34.8f', globs=[...]) -> all-null result fields + 'this worktree is already bound to 34.8g, which is still open'. The same claim from the shell inside its own tree succeeded. EXPECTED: ddflow_claim takes a 'cwd'/'worktree' argument (Claude Code subagents can pass their own path), and the MCP instructions tell subagents to pass it; with as_agent set and no cwd, never adopt the connection's tree. Also: the all-null result object on refusal should be an explicit refusal with exit/status 3, not nulls.

ddflow review: chunk accounting is wrong and there is no way to re-review one chunk. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.8f, reviewer lan-<served-model>): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8f review 34.8f --gate rubber_duck' -> 'PARTIAL: 0 finding(s), 6/9 chunk(s) reviewed ... chunk 5/9: TRUNCATED' exit 3 - only ONE failing chunk named for THREE unreviewed; an earlier run said 8/9 with the same single reason. The same chunk (the core module) truncated deterministically in 3 runs of 25-40 min each; with no '--chunk N' / '--paths <files>' option the agent had to bypass ddflow with a direct model call to cover the file, and then recorded the gate passed from that out-of-band call (ddflow cannot verify it). EXPECTED: list every unreviewed chunk with cause + file list; add 'ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk N' or '--paths' to re-run a subset and MERGE coverage into the gate outcome; on deterministic truncation, auto-split the chunk.

publish.yml mcp-registry job makes exactly one 'mcp-publisher publish' attempt, so a transient registry-side 504 (nginx 60s gateway timeout; upstream modelcontextprotocol/registry#1444, fix PR #1562 open: publish requests starve in the DB pool) fails the release and skips the tag job, though PyPI and both images shipped. Seen in publish #38 (0.1.6): manifest valid (PyPI README carries mcp-name, docker.io and ghcr.io images carry the io.modelcontextprotocol.server.name label, both resolve in ~1s), registry health 200, yet 504 after 60s and /v0.1/servers/io.github.delian%2Fddflow-mcp/versions/0.1.6 is 404 afterwards. Versions 0.1.4-0.1.6 are on PyPI and Docker with no git tag and no registry entry. Needs: retry with backoff, a check after each failure whether the version landed anyway (a 504 can hide a commit), and treating an already-published version as success.

title: mcp-registry publish survives a transient registry 504: retry with backoff, check the registry for the exact version after each failure, fail with a clear error only after the budget (fixes bug B-mcp-registry-504)

body: ddflow merge leaves the PRIMARY checkout mid-merge on a conflict (and doctor/recover don't notice), blocking every later merge by every agent. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): main had just landed 34.8f (5c2bcce, adds a CHANGELOG line); 'ddflow --agent impl-34.6e merge 34.6e' from the agent's worktree printed 'Auto-merging configs/default.toml / Auto-merging docs/CHANGELOG.md / CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in docs/CHANGELOG.md / Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.' The primary (/ai/delian/src/home-simulator, on main) was left with MERGE_HEAD, 12 staged files and unmerged docs/CHANGELOG.md. Any later 'ddflow merge' fails with 'Merging is not possible because you have unmerged files'. 'ddflow doctor' -> 'Healthy'; 'ddflow recover --item 34.6e' -> 'Nothing to recover'. The agent is (correctly) forbidden from touching the primary, so the queue is wedged until an operator runs 'git merge --abort' there (done; then the same merge landed as 2166949 once the branch already contained main). EXPECTED: merge runs with a conflict check first (git merge-tree --write-tree, or merge --no-commit then abort on conflict), ALWAYS leaves the primary clean, exits 3 with 'merge main into your branch and retry'; doctor flags MERGE_HEAD/unmerged paths in the primary; test: conflicting branch -> exit 3 and primary has no MERGE_HEAD.

MCP ddflow_merge fails its own commit_without_lease hook for an ADOPTED worktree: merge commits in the PRIMARY checkout, where the hook derives the agent id from the primary tree (<host>-run_nemo_run-*), not the lease holder's (<host>-bridge-cse_...-d42835). Output: every staged path '<-- held by 159.A.8 (<my id>)' yet 'You hold: (no live lease)', 'STOP: leased by ANOTHER agent', and the primary is LEFT MID-MERGE (MERGE_HEAD set, changes staged, 'Not committing merge') while the MCP result reports sha ''. Workaround: git merge --abort in the primary, then DDFLOW_AGENT=<holder> ddflow merge <id>. Fix: merge should run the commit with DDFLOW_AGENT=<the merging identity>, and abort its own merge on any failure (never leave the primary checkout mid-merge). Seen run_nemo_run 159.A.8, 2026-10-01.

review: default [[reviewer]].max_concurrency=4 is below chunks x hedge for any diff over ~2 chunks, so a review runs in WAVES and takes ~the sum of its slowest chunk per wave. Measured on run_nemo_run 2026-10-01 (LAN <served-model>, 5 chunks x hedge 2): 1301-1465 s at 4 vs 1122 s at max_concurrency=12 (one wave; floor = the runaway chunk's timeout). Suggest: default to chunks*hedge capped by a per-server limit, or warn when max_concurrency < chunks*hedge.

review: a chunk whose model exhausts max_tokens is reported 'unreachable: timed out' when timeout_s fires first (32000 tokens at <36 tok/s > 900 s), which reads as an endpoint problem. On run_nemo_run 159.A.8 the chunk DETERMINISTICALLY ran to max_tokens (5/5; finish_reason=length; low effort, thinking off, smaller chunks and a stop-rule prompt all failed) -- hedge copies only double the wasted compute. Suggest: label it 'did not converge (finish_reason=length / budget)', record tokens + finish_reason per chunk in evidence, and skip hedge retries of a chunk whose first copy hit length.

review: services.review.review() takes extra_rules and review_system.md renders a 'Project-specific rules' block, but no caller ever passes extra_rules (grep: only the parameter default) and no config key feeds it -- a dead knob; a project can only change reviewer instructions by overriding the whole template. Wire it from config (e.g. [review].extra_rules / a file path) or delete the parameter and the template block.

'ddflow show <bug id>' answers "no such item" for a recorded bug (REPRO 2026-10-01: ddflow show B-mcp-registry-504 and ddflow show B-mcp-registry-ownership both -> no such item, exit 1, though both have bug.found events), so a bug's summary, fix task and regression test can be read only by grepping .ddflow/events or via recall; the brief's own footer says '`ddflow show <id>` for detail' and agents are handed bug ids to show. Expected: show resolves a bug id (summary, state, fixing item, regression test) or names the command that does.

Long-running 'ddflow review' does not renew the caller's lease, so an item expires mid-review and ddflow offers overlapping work as READY. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): impl-34.8h (lease ttl_s=1800) committed and started 'ddflow review 34.8h --gate rubber_duck/critic' against the LAN DeepSeek reviewer (25-40 min per run). Lease expired during the review; 'ddflow wait --item 34.8i' then returned 'woke: 34.8h: lease expired / READY: 34.8i', and 'ddflow next' listed 34.8h as INTERRUPTED ('run ddflow recover') and 34.8i (which writes the SAME file home_simulator/behavior/button_trigger_goals.py) as ready - an agent following next would start a conflicting edit while 34.8h's owner is alive and about to merge. EXPECTED: review (and any long ddflow-run command: gate run unit_tests) heartbeats the lease of the item it is working on while it runs; and/or 'next' should not offer an item whose overlap is with an item whose worktree has commits ahead of main within the last N minutes without a warning.

tests/test_api_layer.py::test_a_migrated_tool_reproduces_its_CLI_json_exactly[ddflow_companions] probes the real machine's companions twice (once per surface) and compares the results, so it fails whenever one probe is inconclusive and the other is not. Seen in the pre-push hook on main a91ac5c under -n 48: the CLI's 'npx --no-install @upstash/context7-mcp --help' exceeded DETECT_TIMEOUT_S (20s) -> state unknown, the MCP call's answered -> installed; push refused. The parity check must compare surfaces, not two live probes: seed the probe cache (.ddflow/local/companion-probes.json) with fixed results so neither call shells out.

Fixes bug B-flaky-companions-parity. The parametrised CLI-vs-MCP parity test runs 'companions list' on each surface; each probes the real companions (npx, docker, cargo tools) with a 20s timeout, so under load one probe times out (unknown) and the other answers (installed) and the comparison fails. Seed .ddflow/local/companion-probes.json with a fixed result for every companion id before either call: both surfaces read the cache, nothing shells out, and the comparison is of surfaces, not of two probes.
title: The companions surface-parity test seeds the probe cache instead of probing the machine twice (fixes bug B-flaky-companions-parity)

body: ddflow merge run from inside the item's worktree merges successfully ('merged B-fix-flaky-companions-parity (463d910e) into main'), then removes that worktree and exits 1 with 'pwd: [REDACTED] retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories' -- a successful merge reported as a failure, so a script or agent checking the exit code retries or stops on a merge that landed.

brief shows the wrong 'Current' item for an agent: right after 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8h claim 34.8h' (exit 0), 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8h brief' (exit 0) was headed 'Current: C11' - an item impl-34.8h never claimed (C11 was the top ready item / the SessionStart brief's pick for the parent session). 'ddflow brief --item 34.8h' is correct. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01). EXPECTED: with an --agent identity holding a live lease, brief's Current is that lease's item; only fall back to the top ready item when the agent holds nothing, and label it 'Suggested next' rather than 'Current'.

complete refuses with an EMPTY author model unless --model is passed, though the agent's session declared one. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8h complete 34.8h' -> exit 3 'reviewer independence not satisfied: the author's model '' is not in [agent].families'. The agent had earlier run 'ddflow session start --model claude-opus'. Passing '--model claude-opus' to complete makes it pass. EXPECTED: complete defaults the author model from the agent's open session (or from the claim, which could record it), and the refusal message says 'pass --model <author model>' instead of quoting an empty string.

Fixes bug B226d8db6e8: api.brief with no --item took plan.ready[0] and rendered it as 'Current', even when the agent held a live lease on another item. Now: no --item -> the agent's own live leases; one -> it is Current; several -> Current is the most recently claimed and the rest are listed; none -> ready[0] rendered as 'Suggested next'. Same for MCP ddflow_brief (as_agent flows through api.brief). Fixes bug B7a5c63e3d2: api.complete with no --model passed '' to reviewer_independence; now defaults to the model of the agent's most recent open session (session start --model), on both surfaces since both call api.complete; when still unknown the refusal says to pass --model <author model> instead of quoting ''. MCP clientInfo carries the harness name, not a model, so it is not a source.
title: A command under an --agent identity uses what that agent holds: brief's Current is the agent's own lease (else 'Suggested next'), complete defaults the author model from the agent's open session (fixes bugs B226d8db6e8, B7a5c63e3d2)

body: Fixes bug B227585c781. bug fixed --regression-test splits its value on ',' only, so 'a.py::t1;a.py::t2' is resolved as ONE node id and refused as 'names a test that exists in no worktree: <the whole string>' -- the input is misdiagnosed. The flag is also not repeatable: '--regression-test a --regression-test b' silently records only b. Fix: the flag appends (repeatable); each value is split on ',' and ';' outside parametrize brackets; MCP accepts the existing string and also a JSON list; every test is resolved and a refusal names only the missing ones (and how many of how many), with a hint when one entry looks like several tests joined by whitespace. The event keeps regression_test (the given string verbatim, or ', '-joined from a list -- back-compat for every reader: fold, index, bug invalid's message, CLI echo) and adds regression_tests (the split list).
title: bug fixed accepts several regression tests: repeatable --regression-test, ';' or ',' separated, a list over MCP; a missing one is named alone (fixes bug B227585c781)

body: Fixes bugs B9f8019c521 and B1172da8c35. (1) merge's result and its worktree.merged event carry sha = the commit the base now points at (the merge commit; the branch head on a fast-forward), matching what the PR path already records (info.merge_sha); the branch's head moves to branch_head. complete without --sha reports the merge commit it records. (2) ddflow merge itself exits 0 when run from inside the item's worktree; the exit 1 + 'pwd: [REDACTED] is the CALLING shell's post-command pwd failing in the directory merge just deleted. Merge now keeps the worktree when the caller (CLI cwd, or called_from) stands in it, says so and where to cd, and that cleanup --apply removes it once complete.
title: merge reports the merge commit on the base as sha (branch head as branch_head), and keeps a worktree the caller stands in instead of deleting its shell's directory (fixes bug B9f8019c521, B1172da8c35)

body: Follow-up to B-fix-asagent-claim (89fa18e), which made only ddflow_claim ignore the connection's called_from for a per-call as_agent naming someone else. (1) MCP: every other tool that reads called_from (gate_run, gate_record, review, merge, tests, precommit, heartbeat) still resolved a subagent's call against the PARENT's harness tree: for an item claimed --no-worktree, gate_run ran the parent's tree as the subagent's pass and merge landed the parent's branch. Fix: the dispatcher asks every wants_called_from tool from the primary for a foreign as_agent -- the item's own tree/branch decides; with none, the existing 'name --branch' / unavailable answers apply, as from the CLI in the primary. MCP knows the connection's identity, so this is unconditional. (2) CLI: 'ddflow --agent X claim' from a linked worktree adopted it whatever X was. The CLI has no connection identity, and a named agent adopting its OWN harness-isolated tree is established, tested behaviour (test_cleanup_respects_leases, test_lease_tree_identity claim with --agent worker/lead from a harness tree and expect adoption) -- so 'never adopt under a foreign --agent' is not an option. Rule: the tree is someone else's when the identity derived from it is not the caller AND that identity has written to the log (somebody works there under it -- the parent session's case); then the claim is answered as from the primary (a tree of its own) and says 'not adopted: ...'. No --agent, --agent naming the tree's identity, or a named agent in a tree whose derived identity never wrote, still adopt. Known limit: a tree whose occupant has never written under its derived identity is indistinguishable from a harness-isolated agent's fresh tree. B5c32cbb5c1 (home-simulator) is the same defect as B7c7a0d9222 plus its merge/review consequence.
title: A subagent's identity resolves the item's tree on every surface: MCP tools under a foreign as_agent ask from the primary, and 'ddflow --agent X claim' does not adopt a tree another identity is working in (fixes bugs B11e4c5a185, B5c32cbb5c1)

body: The commit hook says 'You hold: (no live lease)' and prescribes 'ddflow claim' when the committer's own lease, bound to the very tree being committed in, has merely LAPSED (no heartbeat past ttl_s+grace) and nobody has taken it over. check_commit only looks at active_leases, so it cannot say the lease lapsed or name the remedy (heartbeat it as its holder). Seen on B-local-config-surfaces at 4dd7b3e (lease last renewed 14:13:52, commit 15:00:03) and misdiagnosed as an identity bug (B5fde61b8a9, research R2440394451). Expected: name the lapsed lease, when, and 'ddflow --agent <holder> heartbeat <id>'; still warn/refuse per policy.

Fixes B3e050cb66a (and B5fde61b8a9, refuted as an identity bug by R2440394451: the real cause was a lapsed lease): check_commit also scans expired, not-taken-over leases that would have been mine (holder == me or bound to the committing tree) covering an uncovered path, and no other live lease overlaps; names when it lapsed, 'ddflow --agent <holder> heartbeat <id>', and for a tree-only match the takeover path (recover, release, claim). Fixes B9aeb141b9a: its root cause (claim via as_agent recording the parent's tree) was B5c32cbb5c1 = B7c7a0d9222, fixed in 89fa18e1; DDFLOW_AGENT is honoured by the hook (tested end to end); what remained is the message blaming the holder: when nothing declared an identity and the path is held by another lease, the hook says it derived the name from the tree and, per holder, where its item's tree is and DDFLOW_AGENT=<holder>. Fixes Bf1fc9823fe: test_a_claimed_commit_succeeds_with_no_agent_configured_anywhere scrubs DDFLOW_AGENT for its claim too. Outcomes unchanged (warn/block per policy).
title: The commit hook names a lapsed lease of this tree or agent with its heartbeat/takeover remedy, says how it named an undeclared committer and how a holder outside its tree is covered; the no-agent hook test scrubs DDFLOW_AGENT (fixes bugs B3e050cb66a, B9aeb141b9a, Bf1fc9823fe)

body: ddflow review has no wall-clock timeout/progress, and auto-records 'failed' before triage. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item C12, reviewer lan-<served-model>): 'ddflow --agent impl-C12 review C12 --gate critic' on a 9 KB diff produced NO output for >15 min and had to be killed (the rubber_duck review of the same diff on the same endpoint finished in ~4 min). Nothing was recorded, so the gate was left silent until the agent recorded 'unavailable' by hand. Separately, 'ddflow review C12 --gate rubber_duck' auto-recorded the gate as FAILED because the reviewer emitted 3 MEDIUM findings - all three were refuted by probes and the agent had to re-record 'passed' with evidence, leaving a failed->passed flip in the log that reads like a fix happened. EXPECTED: (1) per-chunk and total timeouts ([[reviewer]].timeout_s) with streamed progress ('chunk 2/3 ...'), recording 'unavailable' on timeout; (2) record findings as 'findings_pending_triage' (or partial) and let the author resolve each finding (confirmed/refuted with probe) before the gate becomes failed/passed.

gate run keeps only out[-2000:] plus a digest of output it then DISCARDS (services/gates.py ~976), so the digest can never be checked and anything before the last 2 KB is lost. For a gate command that reruns its failures (run_nemo_run's ddflow_test_gate.sh: parallel pass, then --lf serial rerun), the evidence shows only the rerun ('112 passed ... PASSED') and hides that the first pass had ~115 failures -- a red signal silently converted to a green record. Fix: write the full output to a per-run log (e.g. .ddflow/runs/<item>/<gate>-<ts>.log, git-ignored) and record its path next to the digest; optionally surface the gate's own summary lines (pytest '=== N failed' lines) from the whole output, not the tail.

A lease.renewed event overwrites the lease's claimed globs with the item's STORED globs ~10 s after claim. EVIDENCE (home-simulator .ddflow/events/impl-34.10g.jsonl, 2026-10-01): 16:29:30 lease.acquired globs=11 paths (claim --globs, deliberately WITHOUT home_simulator/ontology/archetypes.py, which another agent held); 16:29:30 lease.renewed globs=same 11; 16:29:40 lease.renewed (no data) followed in the SAME second by lease.renewed globs=the item's original 4 (matter_15.py, archetypes.py, tests/test_matter_camera_dem.py, docs/stages/transport-realism.md). Between those only 'gate record' and 'heartbeat' ran. Effects: (a) the lease silently claimed archetypes.py the agent had avoided -> phantom overlap against another agent; (b) the 7 files actually being written fell out of conflict detection; (c) the pre-commit hook then warned '6 staged path(s) are not covered by a lease you hold. You hold: matter_15.py, archetypes.py, ...'. Fixed only when the agent ran 'update --globs' (17:28). EXPECTED: claim --globs also writes task.updated globs (single source of truth), and no renew path re-derives globs from the item; test: claim with globs != stored, heartbeat, then show -> lease globs unchanged.

wait --item reports READY based on the item's stored globs, not the globs the agent will claim with, so the following claim is refused. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10g wait --item 34.10g' printed 'READY: 34.10g' exit 0; the immediately following 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10g claim 34.10g --globs "...,docs/RESEARCH.md,..."' exited 3 on a docs/RESEARCH.md overlap with a live lease. EXPECTED: 'wait' accepts --globs (same parser as claim) and waits for those, or claim/wait share the stored globs once B(claim --globs writes item globs) is fixed; READY should mean 'a claim with these globs will succeed now'.

Lease model has no notion of shared append-only/generated files, so every parallel item collides on them and the commit hook's warning becomes noise. EVIDENCE (home-simulator 2026-10-01, 7 parallel items): docs/CHANGELOG.md, docs/RESEARCH.md, README.md and configs/default.toml (regenerated) are touched by EVERY item. 'ddflow update 34.8i --globs "...,configs/default.toml,..."' -> exit 3 (held by 34.10g); agents therefore committed these files without a lease and got 'not covered by a lease' warnings on every commit; the real collisions on them surfaced only as git conflicts at merge (one of which wedged the primary, B6926ec1ad9). Also: 'git commit' of a merge-from-main commit (5301005 in 34.8i's worktree) warned '17 staged path(s) are not covered by a lease you hold' listing main's already-merged changes (_dag_schema.py, matter_15.py, ...). EXPECTED: (1) a [lease].shared_globs (or 'append' class) list that may be held by many agents at once and is merged with a union/3-way strategy (git merge=union for CHANGELOG-style files, regenerate for generated ones); (2) the pre-commit lease check ignores paths whose staged content equals the merge parent from the base branch (i.e. merge commits from main).

gate record: '--outcome partial' requires --reason but help doesn't say so. REPRO: 'ddflow gate record 34.8i rubber_duck --outcome partial --model <served-model> --evidence "8/11 chunks..."' -> exit 1 "outcome 'partial' must carry a --reason"; 'ddflow gate record --help' lists --reason without saying it is required for partial/unavailable/skipped. EXPECTED: document the requirement in --help (and the MCP schema description), or accept --evidence as the reason when --reason is absent.

tests/test_enforce.py::test_a_claimed_commit_succeeds_with_no_agent_configured_anywhere fails whenever DDFLOW_AGENT is set in the environment running pytest (the hook attributes the commit to that agent, not the holder): the test claims 'no agent configured anywhere' but does not scrub DDFLOW_AGENT. Repro: DDFLOW_AGENT=someone uv run pytest tests/test_enforce.py::test_a_claimed_commit_succeeds_with_no_agent_configured_anywhere -> 1 failed; passes with env -u DDFLOW_AGENT. Hits any agent that exports DDFLOW_AGENT as the driver advises.

ddflow decision list (human output) crashes with KeyError: 'live': surfaces/commands/decisions.py:_decision_list reads d['live'] but api.decisions.decision_list builds rows with _plain(d), which carries 'status' and no 'live' key (live is a property). --json works. Probe: main 028b910, 'ddflow decision list' -> KeyError: 'live'.

Decision D-reviewer-trust (operator 2026-10-01, option C), bug B3f9b8a4ac0, research Re2a7e01d8e. (1) configwrite (_write_config, _append_config, append_block -- every tool write of config/reviewers) refuses a NEW or CHANGED kind='command' reviewer unless the caller is a person: the CLI with no agent identity (no --agent, no DDFLOW_AGENT, not inside an agent harness). MCP ddflow_configure and reviewers detect never are. (2) Every tool write that creates or changes a reviewer's identity (name, kind, base_url, model, family, command) appends reviewer.configured {name, digest, kind, by agent}. (3) gate evidence written by ddflow review carries reviewer_digest (stamped in gates.record from the configured entry). (4) reviewer_independence does not count a review whose digest a tool wrote and no person approved. (5) 'ddflow reviewers approve <name>' (CLI only, refused under an agent identity, like human gates) appends reviewer.approved {name, digest, by OS user}. Back-compat: an entry with no reviewer.configured event for its digest is operator-written and counts as before; evidence without a digest (recorded before this) counts as before.
title: Agents cannot mint an independent reviewer: agent surfaces refuse to write a kind='command' [[reviewer]]; a tool-written HTTP reviewer is recorded (reviewer.configured, agent + entry digest) and its reviews count only after a person runs 'ddflow reviewers approve <name>' (decision D-reviewer-trust, fixes bug B3f9b8a4ac0)

body: Research R-stale-after-merge. Gates record a content id of the tree they ran on (source_tree: every path's mode+blob id, .ddflow/ excluded, computed without writing objects) next to tree_sha. complete compares it against the item's worktree while one exists, and after merge (worktree removed, or claimed without one) against the merged branch head (second parent of the landing merge commit, else the landed commit) instead of the primary checkout. Legacy evidence with only tree_sha 'X+clean' compares commit X's content. The NOTE says what differs (the files, when knowable). Only a real difference warns.
title: complete's stale-evidence NOTE compares content trees, and after merge compares against the branch that landed, naming what differs (fixes bugs Bd86b05a8f8, Ba84119f707, B613cb67194)

body: Research R-gate-run-output-lost. run_command_gate writes the whole output to .ddflow/runs/<item>/<gate>-<ts>.log (a self-ignoring directory) and records output_log next to output_digest, so the digest can be checked; summary lines (pytest '=== N failed ... ===', unittest 'FAILED (...)') from the WHOLE output are recorded, so a rerun-on-failure gate cannot hide its first pass behind the tail. gate record records --output-file's path as well.
title: gate run keeps its full output in a per-run log next to the digest and lifts the suite's summary lines from the whole output; gate record keeps --output-file's path (fixes bug Bac392907b1)

body: Bug B7506c1124a. config._coerce_dict returns {str(k): str(v)} for a JSON object given to a dict[str, str] knob, so DDFLOW_AGENT_FAMILIES='{"core": null}' loads as {'core': 'None'} and a reviewer named 'core' is classified family 'none'; _coerce's list branch does the same ([null] -> ['None'], [1] -> ['1']). Fix: a JSON value that is not a string is refused with a ValueError naming the key and the JSON type, as the dict[str, list[str]] branch already does. Regression tests in tests/test_env_json_values.py (through Config.load with an env dict, and _coerce directly).
title: A string-valued map or list knob set from the environment as JSON refuses a non-string value instead of str()-casting it (null -> 'None') (fixes bug B7506c1124a)

body: Bug B768503a43a: _registered_name counts servers.get(cid) is not None, so {} / "x" / 5 / [] under the id read as registered: Status.usable True, gate_coverage counts the gate as served, while register() would write (its == want check fails) -- reader and writer disagree. Fix: an id entry counts only when _launch_of(entry) is not None or it carries a url (remote server); the TOML substring check likewise must not count a header whose table launches nothing. Regression test fails on main: each junk value -> state != registered, gate uncovered.
title: companions: an entry under a companion's id counts as registered only when it can launch something (fixes bug B768503a43a)

body: Research Rbae79a9bc8. _judge_any returns 'blocked' over every live lease whenever another agent holds anything, without asking whether any blocked item could clear on a release. Judge each blocker: WAITABLE reasons (conflict, deps, resources) and a full parallelism cap can clear; cycle, expired (reclaim_policy=report) and the rest need a person. When none can clear, return hopeless with the reasons, like the single-item wait.
title: An any-wait whose every blocker needs an operator (cycle, expired lease under report) refuses at once instead of sleeping to its timeout (fixes bug B02e99efc75)

body: B13ed484062: critical_path(state, phase) filters on direct parentage; use the phase plus its descendants (as plan does via state.tasks). B40386f7a40: plan's cap blocker says 'parallelism cap reached' even when slots are free; when slots > 0 say how many are free and which higher-ranked items take them. Bdcce70d036: status counts blocked only for reason 'deps', so cap-held items are in no bucket; plan records the cap-held ids, status reports tasks.held_by_cap and counts every other non-ready reason as blocked so total == done + running + ready + held_by_cap + blocked (+ review/abandoned/interrupted as they apply), and brief/status prose say 'N more ready but held by max_parallel_tasks=K'. Regression tests in tests/test_schedule_cap_reporting.py fail on current main.
title: Scheduler reporting: critical_path walks nested sub-tasks; the cap message says when a slot is free; status/brief count cap-held items (fixes bugs B13ed484062, B40386f7a40, Bdcce70d036)

body: B289bf87e8d: Reviewer.max_concurrency=4 < chunks x hedge for any diff over 2 chunks, so a review runs in waves (measured 1301-1465 s at 4 vs 1122 s at 12 on 5 chunks x hedge 2). Fix: default 0 = auto, every chunk's copies in one wave (chunks x hedge), bounded by a generic ceiling; a positive value is an explicit cap for a server with few slots. B568e9def3b / B769704d1dc: a reasoning-model reviewer spends max_tokens reasoning and returns no verdict. Lesson Lf3feebf5d3 measured the root cause: at ddflow's default temperature 0.3 DeepSeek loops ('let me reconsider') to the budget on every reasoning_effort; at 1.0 the same diff reviewed fully. The operator's other projects' reviewer entries carry no temperature, so they run at 0.3. Fix (generic, no local values): temperature defaults to unset and is then OMITTED from the request, so the server applies the model's own recommended sampling (vLLM: generation_config; APIs: their default); an explicit value is still sent. The TRUNCATED message names temperature first. A chunk whose every copy came back TRUNCATED is retried once, split in halves when it splits (else whole), within total_budget_s; chunks_total and reporting are unchanged. Tests: tests/test_reviewer_defaults.py.
title: Reviewer defaults fit reasoning models: temperature unset by default (the model's own), max_concurrency 0 = one wave of chunks x hedge, a chunk whose every copy truncated is retried once in halves, TRUNCATED names the temperature remedy; a hedged copy cut off mid-read no longer crashes the review (fixes bugs B289bf87e8d, B568e9def3b, B769704d1dc, Bf948d29d37)

body: services/review.py + api/review.py. (1) B779270c994: split_diff keeps the newline with a file's header, so a file larger than max_chunk_chars is never sent as a header-only chunk (R1dc7a03312). (2) Bbf41d8f07f: the text git appends after a hunk header's closing @@ (its funcname guess, often a line from ANOTHER block) is stripped before the diff reaches a reviewer (Rc33e00d805). (3) Bd2332f8f2a part 1: a PARTIAL/UNAVAILABLE result names EVERY unreviewed chunk with its cause and its files, and evidence carries them (R26b16478ef). Re-splitting a truncated chunk is B-fix-reviewer-defaults' (fix-reviewer-config); the --chunk re-review that merges coverage is a follow-up task (needs cli.py/mcp.py). (4) B338a8bb598: a read timeout after the endpoint accepted the request reads 'did not converge within timeout_s' with the remedy, not 'unreachable: timed out'; a reply cut at max_tokens with text but no STATUS is reported TRUNCATED (finish_reason=length), not off-contract (Raf403f34b3). Hedging is kept: one copy in four not converging is exactly what hedging is for (Rfa535c6747). (5) B9d8bd466c3 part 1: per-chunk progress lines as each chunk settles and a 'still waiting' line while chunks are in flight; the auto-'failed' policy part needs the operator. (6) Bc6ec4fd40d/Bf0cccb8fb1: review renews the caller's lease on the item every lease.heartbeat_s while it waits, on the caller's thread, only if the caller holds it (gate run already does: R247389c7cd). (7) Bbeb0c7542f: [[reviewer]].extra_rules (text; a per-reviewer knob like system_prompt_path) is rendered into the system prompt's 'Project-specific rules' block.
title: Review chunks: no header-only chunk, no misleading hunk-header context, every unreviewed chunk named with its cause and files, a timed-out generation labelled 'did not converge' (not unreachable), per-chunk progress, the caller's lease renewed while it runs, [[reviewer]].extra_rules reaches the prompt (fixes bugs B779270c994, Bbf41d8f07f, B338a8bb598, Bbeb0c7542f, Bc6ec4fd40d, Bf0cccb8fb1; part of Bd2332f8f2a, B9d8bd466c3)

body: Operator decision needed before any code (research R5d7bf2d721). Today a review with >=1 finding records the gate 'failed' at once; an author who refutes every finding re-records 'passed', and the log reads like a fix happened. D-failed-critic-not-blocking settles that failed does not block complete, not when failed is recorded. Options: (A) keep; (B) new outcome 'findings' pending triage, complete refuses until every finding is resolved -- re-opens 'do not block'; (C, recommended) keep 'failed', add 'ddflow review triage <id> --gate G --finding N --refuted|--confirmed --probe ...' (and MCP) recording a triage event per finding; render a failed gate whose findings are all refuted as 'failed -> triaged: all refuted'. Ask the operator; record the decision; then implement.
title: PROPOSAL (needs operator): a review's findings are triaged before the gate reads as failed -- record per-finding triage (refuted/confirmed + probe) instead of a failed->passed flip (bug B9d8bd466c3 part 2)

body: Decision D-shared-globs (operator, option A, merge=union written automatically). Research R16b7d15f12. (1) config: [lease].shared_globs -- paths many items may edit whose merge ddflow does NOT decide (generated files: regenerate after merging); [lease].append_only_globs -- shared too, and ddflow writes '<glob> merge=union' to .gitattributes for each (CHANGELOG-style files; git probe: two prepends merge cleanly). A generated file never gets merge=union (union interleaves). (2) core/schedule: conflicts() skips a glob inside a shared or append-only glob, on both sides; used by plan's blocker and leases.glob_clash (claim, update, wait). (3) enforce.check_commit: a staged path inside a shared glob counts as covered for any agent holding a live lease. (4) services/shared_files.sync_attributes: idempotent append of the missing union lines (adopt._append_once), returning what it added; called by api.setup.configure after a successful --set/--append-toml (CLI config and MCP ddflow_configure: the moment the setting changes, in the same tree as config.toml, so both land in one commit) and by adopt.init_files (init/adopt, which re-syncs a hand-edited config); each prints the lines it added. (5) doctor: a PROBLEM for an append-only glob whose union line is missing (remedy names the command), a NOTE for a shared glob with no merge attribute in .gitattributes. The commit-hook 'paths a merge from main brought in' warning is a separate task (B-fix-hook-merge-from-base).
title: [lease].shared_globs and [lease].append_only_globs: files many items may hold at once; ddflow writes merge=union for the append-only ones, and doctor warns about a shared generated file with no merge strategy (bug B07878037ab, decision D-shared-globs)

body: Bug B6805b48aca, research R9afca028e2. resolve --keep X sets renewed_at = max(renewed_at, at): a long-lapsed X is treated as held from its claim to the resolution, and claims on record inside that gap are never re-weighed (A(1150,300) E(1200,300) C(150,150) D(250,50), keep D at 5000 -> contest [], A displaced, though A lies in D's widened 250..5050). Options: (a) re-check after widening: A joins a contest with D, the item is contested again right after it was settled, and a resolve of a lapsed claim can never finish in one step. (b) RECOMMENDED: widening is the modelling error -- when the kept claim had lapsed by the resolution's 'at', the resolution starts a new window [at, at+ttl] (the original claim's window stays what pairwise reads use) and only claims overlapping the new window are re-checked; A's claim in the gap was a legitimate takeover. (c) re-check and auto-release newly overlapped claims: releases a claim nobody chose. Regression test: the 24-permutation probe in tests/test_lease_contest.py asserting the chosen outcome. Blocked until the operator picks a model.
title: resolve --keep X: the kept claim's window after a resolution is weighed against the record (fixes bug B6805b48aca) -- NEEDS OPERATOR DECISION

body: A cancelled hedged copy can crash the whole review: _Cancel shuts the losing copy's socket, and when that copy is mid-read of its response, resp.read() raises http.client.IncompleteRead (an HTTPException, not OSError). _chat_openai and _post_json catch HTTPError/URLError/OSError/ValueError only, so it escapes _chat, _race's fut.result() re-raises it, and review() -- documented 'never raises' -- raises. Seen as a ~1-in-3 flake of a two-copy instant-answer test (tests/test_reviewer_defaults.py) on 29adead; pre-existing on main.

Bug Bfeb62112d9: Ctx.repo is the primary (repo_root via --git-common-dir), and setup/adopt write every file under it, so adopt from a worktree dirtied the primary (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .mcp.json, .gitattributes, docs/ddflow) and left the caller's branch with nothing; it also judged .claude/commands/implement.md by the primary's copy. Fix: api.setup takes called_from; files are written into the caller's own tree (--show-toplevel); the log (.ddflow/events under the primary) and the hooks (git common dir) are unchanged. CLI passes called_from; the init report's commit hint and rules check look at that tree. Regression test: adopt from a linked worktree leaves the primary's git status clean and writes into the worktree; fails on current code. MCP ddflow_setup wiring needs surfaces/mcp.py (held by B-fix-asagent-tree).
title: adopt run from a linked worktree writes the project's tracked files into that worktree, not the primary checkout; the shared event log and hooks stay shared (fixes bug Bfeb62112d9)

body: tree_fingerprint never reports 'clean': it joins three parts with NUL and tests body.strip(), which does not strip NUL, so a clean tree gets the digest of '\0\0' (95e0c70caf8cc336) instead of 'clean'. Every recorded tree_sha therefore reads as dirty, and nothing can tell from the evidence that a gate ran on a committed tree. Probe: clean worktree, status/diff/untracked all empty -> tree_fingerprint = '<head>+95e0c70caf8cc336'.

A heartbeat that revives a lapsed lease catches up its globs but not its resources: update --resources made while the lease had lapsed reaches item.resources only (plan_retarget leaves an expired lease alone), and api/lifecycle._catch_up_globs re-syncs globs only, so a raised reservation stays under-counted by resource_shortfall. Fixing it needs claim --resources to write item.resources too (else the catch-up would undo a claim-time override, as Bbd07ab69fd does for globs). Found by roborev job 895 on a7514d8 (B-update-resources-lease); deferred to the claim-globs task because api/lifecycle.py is held elsewhere.

CLI cannot tell a parent's harness tree from a subagent's own when the parent uses a DECLARED identity. B-fix-asagent-tree (services/tree_owner.py) treats a linked tree as another identity's only when the identity DERIVED from it has written to the log. A parent session that always passes --agent/DDFLOW_AGENT never writes under the derived id, so 'ddflow --agent sub-1 claim T1' from the parent's tree still adopts it (roborev probe on 61eb669: ADOPTED: True, branch parent-work). Needs a structured owner of a harness tree (e.g. recorded at first claim/adoption or session start from that tree) rather than inference from which id happened to write. Design choice: operator decision.

MCP refusals render an all-null result object: a refused ddflow_claim returns content[0] = {item: null, holder: null, worktree: null, ...} and isError false, with the reason only in a second text block and exit 3 only in _meta. A subagent reads the nulls as a broken success (home-simulator Bf05ce67c54's second ask). Probe on 5d02642: Server(called_from=tree); claim T1 (adopts); claim T2 -> {'item': null, ... } + 'this worktree is already bound to T1' and _meta.exit 3. Expected: a refusal's first block is the refusal (outcome refused, reason, exit 3), not the success schema filled with nulls.

companions add never refreshes a stale TOML (codex) entry under the companion's id: .codex/config.toml '[mcp_servers.context7]\ncommand = "old-launcher"' -> register returns ('unchanged', 'already registers context7') and leaves the stale command, while the JSON branch compares the entry with the launch it would write and rewrites it. Pre-existing on main (it returned unchanged on the header text); found by roborev job 902 on B-fix-companions-id-entry. Fix needs a TOML table rewrite (remove the old table, append the new) or an honest 'differs; fix by hand' message.

MCP ddflow_setup run by a server standing in a linked worktree still writes the project's tracked files into the PRIMARY checkout: B-fix-adopt-in-worktree gave api.setup a called_from (CLI adopt/init pass it), but the ddflow_setup spec in surfaces/mcp.py has no wants_called_from, so it calls adopt_project with called_from=None. Reproduced by roborev (job 908): Server(repo, called_from=worktree) ddflow_setup -> ?? AGENTS.md/.mcp.json/.ddflow/config.toml in the primary, nothing in the worktree. Fix: wants_called_from on ddflow_setup and pass it through; an MCP mirror of tests/test_adopt_from_worktree.py. mcp.py was held by B-fix-asagent-tree.

Bug B1e7ad10c6c: give the ddflow_setup spec 'wants_called_from': True and pass called_from to adopt_project (api.setup already takes it, B-fix-adopt-in-worktree). Regression test: Server(repo, called_from=<linked worktree>) ddflow_setup leaves the primary's git status free of committed files and writes AGENTS.md/.mcp.json/.ddflow/config.toml into the worktree; fails on current code.
title: MCP ddflow_setup writes into the tree the server stands in, as CLI adopt does (fixes bug B1e7ad10c6c)

body: Flaky: tests/test_subtasks.py::test_splitting_finished_work_is_refused failed once in a -n 48 full run (worktree B-fix-schedule-cap-reporting at e0cbc98, 2887 passed): pass_pipeline's 'gate status P1.T1' answered "no such item 'P1.T1'" right after _proj added it and claim ran; the next full run at b43082b passed. _proj ignores every run_cli return code, so a setup step that failed under load (init/phase/task add) surfaces later as a missing item; first step is to assert the setup exit codes so the real failing command is named.

Bug B695d7925bf. _install_one refuses over any foreign hook with 'Add this line to it yourself'. For a hook carrying the pre-commit framework header: if armed() says the framework already runs ddflow's check at that stage, report that and install nothing (not a refusal); otherwise refuse with the config-side remedy armed() already computes (a repo: local hook in the config named by the hook's ARGS line; ddflow precommit proposes one), never the generated file. --force unchanged. Regression test: generated hook + config without ddflow entries -> refusal names .pre-commit-config.yaml and not 'Add this line to it yourself'; with ddflow entries -> exit 0 and nothing overwritten. Fails on current code.
title: hooks install over a pre-commit-framework hook advises a repo: local hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml, not an edit the next pre-commit install discards, and does not refuse when the framework already runs ddflow's check (fixes bug B695d7925bf)

body: REGRESSION (appeared within the last ~15 min of merges: 0c3682c B-fix-hook-lapsed-lease / d84f0da B-fix-adopt-in-worktree): 'hooks check-commit' reports 'You hold: (no live lease)' for a LIVE lease in an ADOPTED worktree, even with DDFLOW_AGENT set to the holder, so every commit there is refused. Repro on run_nemo_run, worktree .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01U9DjDUKdeBwFUH8KpT4Cju (adopted by claim, here=true): 'ddflow show 159.A.9' -> 'lease <host>-bridge-cse_01U9DjDUKdeBwFUH8KpT4Cju-d42835 (1736s left)'; 'DDFLOW_AGENT=<host>-bridge-cse_01U9DjDUKdeBwFUH8KpT4Cju-d42835 scripts/ddflow_hook.sh hooks check-commit' with dag_schema.py staged (inside the item's globs) -> '2 staged path(s) are not covered by a lease you hold ... You hold: (no live lease)'. The same worktree committed fine ~1h earlier (27b58e26). Blocks all work in adopted worktrees; --no-verify is forbidden by the repo.

Fixes bug B9811d8617c. 'ddflow brief --agent X --item Y' fails 'unrecognized arguments: --agent' because the global options exist only on the root parser; agents naturally append flags and the drivers say 'pass --agent on every call' without saying where. Fix: after build_parser, add --repo/--agent/--json to every (nested) subparser with default=SUPPRESS, so a value given after the subcommand sets the same dest and an absent one does not overwrite a value given before it. Test both positions for each option, nested subcommands (gate run, bug found), and that a value before the subcommand survives.
title: Global --agent, --repo and --json are accepted after the subcommand too (fixes bug B9811d8617c)

body: schedule.critical_path ignores an umbrella's sub-tasks: P1.T1 split into sub-task P1.T1a, P1.T2 needs P1.T1 -> critical_path == ['P1.T1','P1.T2'], though T1 closes only when T1a does, so the real chain is T1a -> T1 -> T2 and the reported wall-clock floor is one short per nesting level. longest() walks inherited_deps only; an umbrella's open descendants are not edges. Found writing tests/test_board_json.py (B-fix-board-json).

Bug Bec8d5228c9, decided by the operator as D-sticky-binding-remedy (A + B + D; C rejected as redundant). Reproduced on main 92a49f9: an item bound to the wrong tree (bridge-work, 0 commits ahead) re-binds to it on re-claim; merge --branch <real> is refused; plain merge exits 0, records the item merged and lands nothing. (A) merge refuses (exit 3) when the branch it would land has no commits ahead of its target, naming the branch and 'ddflow update <id> --worktree PATH' as the way out; --allow-empty lands it anyway (MCP allow_empty). (B) 'ddflow update <id> --worktree PATH' (MCP worktree) rebinds the item -- and the caller's live lease -- to that linked worktree of this repository and its checked-out branch, recorded as worktree.adopted; refused for a path that is not a linked worktree, a tree bound to another open item, or an item whose live lease another agent holds. (D) complete's stale-evidence check already compares content trees (b347b64); this adds the binding case: evidence recorded after a rebind is measured against the rebound tree, so no false 'different tree' note.
title: A wrong worktree binding can be corrected (update --worktree rebinds), merge refuses to land a branch with nothing on it (--allow-empty), and complete's tree check holds after a rebind (fixes bug Bec8d5228c9)

body: Research Rc6d9f0349e, Rad6c6903f7. (1) leases.acquire / _renew_in_place: globs a claim names that differ from the item's stored globs are appended as <kind>.updated in the same transaction, so item and lease agree and heartbeat's _catch_up_globs (Bb21d338f26) -- on a live lease or one revived after lapsing (Bc5aec031b3, run_nemo_run 159.A.9: revival copied the item's [] over 5 claimed globs) -- has nothing to undo. (2) core/globspec: parse (comma list, JSON array, several values) and problem (a double quote, an edge single quote, an unbalanced '['); leases.acquire refuses a mangled glob with LeaseError (claim exit 3, nothing recorded); items add/update parse with it and refuse a mangled one. Surface half (repeated --globs flag in cli.py, api claim parsing JSON for MCP, claim printing its globs, update naming dropped globs, show printing lease globs, wait --globs) is B-fix-globs-surfaces: cli.py, api/lifecycle.py, commands/lifecycle.py and reporting.py are held by other agents now.
title: A claim keeps the globs it was given: claim --globs is recorded on the item, so no heartbeat -- live or reviving a lapsed lease -- resets the lease to the item's stored globs; a glob left mangled by a JSON array or quoting is refused, and add/update read a JSON array whole (fixes bugs Bbd07ab69fd, Bc5aec031b3)

body: Research Rad6c6903f7, Rbed6d1eead, R0b76d41798, roborev 895 (B7f8060f2f5). Builds on B-fix-claim-globs (core/globspec, claim records item globs). (1) cli.py: --globs on claim/update/task add/phase add/split is repeatable (every value kept, each read by globspec). (2) api claim parses globs with globspec (a JSON array from MCP read whole), and returns the recorded globs; cmd_claim prints them. (3) update --globs keeps REPLACE semantics (a field set, as the implement gate text says since B-fix-bad-mentions); the api returns globs_dropped for a claimed item and the CLI prints them; driver text (docs + template) says 'every glob, old and new -- it replaces the list'. (4) show prints the lease's globs when they differ from the item's. (5) wait --item accepts --globs (claim's parser) and judges glob_clash on them. (6) claim --resources records item.resources like globs, and heartbeat's catch-up includes resources through plan_retarget's capacity check. Files are held by B-fix-merge-report / B-fix-global-opts-anywhere / B-fix-board-json right now; claim when they release.
title: Globs on every surface say what was given and what is held: a repeated --globs flag keeps every value, claim prints the globs it recorded, api claim reads a JSON array whole (MCP), update --globs names what it dropped, show prints lease globs, wait --globs judges the claim to come, a revived lease catches up resources too (fixes bugs Bdc85898c40, Bb3cb64444e, Bd8038b08a1, B7036cf788c, B7f8060f2f5)

body: The board (ddflow board, ddflow_board, render's board.md, and now --json board) lists only tasks under a phase: a task added with no phase never appears. Probe on this repo 2026-10-01: 'ddflow board | grep -c B-fix-schedule-cap-reporting' -> 0 while status counts it (every B-fix-* task here is '(no phase)'). views/markdown.board iterates state.phases() only, and with no phases prints 'No phases yet'. Expected: a '(no phase)' section for phase-less tasks.

Bug Ba11a054309: run_nemo_run's driver copies missed the docs gate line and the ddflow wait guidance and doctor said Healthy. (1) services.adopt.driver_drift: on an adopted project, implement-phase.md and each present delta this ddflow ships, compared byte-for-byte with templates/drivers; doctor adds one NOTE naming them with the refresh remedy. (2) services.adopt.refresh_docs: rewrites implement-phase.md, the deltas already present, the managed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md blocks and the adopted agents' native rules -- nothing else. CLI 'adopt --refresh-docs', MCP ddflow_setup refresh_docs; the rules-drift doctor line names it too, since plain adopt also rewrites MCP launches. Regression test: lagging drivers -> doctor names them (fails today); refresh rewrites them and leaves .mcp.json and the hooks byte-identical.
title: doctor notes driver docs that differ from the templates the running ddflow ships, and 'ddflow adopt --refresh-docs' (ddflow_setup refresh_docs) rewrites only the driver docs and rules blocks -- no MCP launch, hook or command-file changes (fixes bug Ba11a054309)

body: Bug Bba19573760, research CONFIRMED: with a 2 s pause before the first 'job end' the test fails exactly as reported (a running job was recorded as ended). The job waits for a release file the test creates after the refusal is checked (bounded at 60 s so a failed test leaves no orphan), so the 'running' assertions no longer race the clock.
title: The detached-job test holds its job open on a release file instead of a 1.5 s sleep (fixes bug Bba19573760)

body: Fixes B6926ec1ad9, Bc50bc7fb58, B9b57176aac. (1) worktree._merge_here: when git merge fails (conflict, or a hook refusing the merge commit) and leaves MERGE_HEAD/a staged merge behind, abort it so the primary is clean, and refuse (exit 3) naming the conflicting files and 'merge <base> into your branch and retry'. (2) enforce.check_commit: a commit concluding a merge (MERGE_HEAD, or the GITHEAD_<sha> env git sets for pre-merge-commit) whose index equals git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD <sha> adds nothing that was not already committed on a parent -- passed without a lease lookup, so neither the primary's derived identity (B9b5) nor pre-commit's stash of the uncommitted lease events (Bc50) can refuse it. A hand-resolved merge is still checked. (3) doctor: a primary with MERGE_HEAD or unmerged paths is a PROBLEM with the remedy.
title: merge never leaves the primary mid-merge, and the commit hook passes a clean merge commit without a lease lookup; doctor flags a primary left mid-merge (fixes bugs B6926ec1ad9, Bc50bc7fb58, B9b57176aac)

body: Regression from B-fix-merge-report (9e775b6, found by roborev job 924): merged_sha is now the landing commit on the merge target, and version planning (services/flow.py, 'merge-base --is-ancestor merged_sha ref') drops a gitflow hotfix from the develop line's plan: the landing merge commit M is on main only, the branch head reached develop by back-merge. roborev reproduced: 'version show' items ['H1'] on b2aa17b, [] on ab90e22. Also the fold drops the new worktree.merged branch_head (Item has no field), so no consumer can use it; and sha silently falls back to the branch head when the base cannot be read.

'ddflow mcp' (the CLI subcommand) starts the server with serve(c.repo) and no called_from, so Server.called_from falls back to the primary: worktree adoption and every called_from-aware tool (merge keeping the caller's tree, gate run, heartbeat) behave as if called from the primary, unlike the ddflow-mcp entry point which passes the caller's cwd (surfaces/cli.py vs surfaces/mcp.py main). Found by roborev job 924.

Research R-gate-reason-help. The MCP schema already says 'Required for failed/unavailable/partial/skipped.'; the CLI's --reason and --outcome carry no help. Add help naming the requirement and what --reason is versus --evidence.
title: gate record --help says --reason is required for failed/unavailable/partial/skipped (fixes bug Be097545791)

body: Bug B-show-bug-id, research R879f3b8b6d CONFIRMED: api.reporting.show looks only in state.items, so 'ddflow show <bug id>' answers 'no such item' (exit 1). show falls back to state.bugs: the record (summary, found/fixed/invalid, regression tests, the item it was found on) plus 'fixing' -- items whose title or body name the bug id. The CLI renders it; MCP ddflow_show returns it as its 'item' payload (no mcp.py change). An id that is neither says 'no such item or bug'.
title: ddflow show / ddflow_show resolve a bug id: summary, state, the items that fix it, regression tests (fixes bug B-show-bug-id)

body: Bug Bd6aa9ffde9, research R6fd65c8791 CONFIRMED: api.reporting.status lists every done task in completed_tasks (721k chars on a 4831-task repo over MCP). status(full=False) cuts completed_tasks (most recent first), ready_now and held_by_cap to a fixed number and says how many there were and that 'ddflow --json status' gives them all; the CLI asks for full=True, so its --json and prose are unchanged. The tasks counts stay exact.
title: MCP ddflow_status is bounded: counts in full, the long lists cut to the most recent with a total and how to get them all (fixes bug Bd6aa9ffde9)

body: Bug Bde0c6e9fad, research Rc253cef829 CONFIRMED: 'ddflow next --phase 159' answers 'Nothing actionable (0 ready, 0 running, 0 blocked)' exit 2 when 159 is not an item, and a driver reads that as 'phase done'. next_ fails (exit 1) on an unknown or removed phase id, naming the items whose id starts with '<id>.' when there are any.
title: next --phase <id> refuses an id that is not an item, naming phases that start with it (fixes bug Bde0c6e9fad)

body: Bug Bb177c2e0e9: surfaces/commands/decisions.py:_decision_list reads d['live'], but api.decisions.decision_list builds rows with core.plain.plain(d), which serialises fields and not the Decision.live property, so the human renderer raised KeyError: 'live' (--json worked). Fix in the API: each row carries live=d.live, so the human view and JSON callers both have it. Regression test drives the CLI handler on a repo with one live and one superseded decision (--all).
title: ddflow decision list prints in human form: every row carries 'live' (fixes bug Bb177c2e0e9)

body: Bug B-import-empty-needed-phase: plan_import keeps a finished phase open work needs (live_phases |= needs) but a plain import leaves its ticked tasks out, so it lands EMPTY and OPEN and 'ddflow next' says '3.B: deps -- phase P5 has no open tasks but is not marked done'. Fix: on the plain path, settle ONLY needed phases with nothing in the plan under them, using _phase_verdict over the ticked tasks the import left out (the source's evidence); the tasks stay out. A phase an earlier plain import left empty-open is completed on a re-run under _settle_existing's rules (imported, still open, untouched since), with 'needed' including the needs of open items already in the queue. Two tests in test_import_done_phases.py relied on P5 landing empty: they now simulate the pre-fix import. Regression tests fail on main.
title: A plain import completes the finished phase open work depends on, so the dependent is offered (fixes bug B-import-empty-needed-phase)

body: Part 1 (B-fix-review-chunks, merged bde10e6) names every unreviewed chunk with its files. Part 2: a deterministic truncation of one chunk forced re-running the WHOLE review (25-40 min) or bypassing ddflow with an unverifiable out-of-band call (home-simulator 34.8f). Design: (1) evidence of every ddflow review gains diff_sha (sha256 of the hunk-context-stripped diff), max_chunk_chars, reviewed (chunk numbers) and findings with their chunk number (detail capped). (2) 'ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk N' (repeatable, or '2,5'); MCP ddflow_review 'chunks'. Chunk numbers are those the last run printed; only those chunks are sent. (3) The result MERGES with the gate's latest record only when that record is a ddflow review of the SAME diff_sha, max_chunk_chars and reviewer; otherwise refused (exit 3) with 'run the full review: the diff or chunking changed'. Merged: reviewed = union; findings = earlier chunks' kept + re-run chunks' replaced; unreviewed = the rest with their earlier reasons; outcome recomputed as a full run would. (4) A chunk number outside 1..N refused. Tests: tests/test_review_rechunk.py. Waits for cli.py/mcp.py (held by B-fix-globs-surfaces at filing time).
title: ddflow review --chunk N re-reviews only the named chunks of the same diff and merges coverage into the gate's recorded outcome (fixes bug Bd2332f8f2a, part 2)

body:
Operator 2026-10-01, verbatim: "Add a feature development to ask agent to check if a bug, or feature for development, task, phase or whatever it adds, is not duplicated and if it is, to preferably update and extend the current content if it is not closed (in case of closed, or working on it - log a new bug, task, whatever, to not lose the changes) so the fix of the other bug to cover the new informantion of there is any. The idea is that we want to prevent duplication as much as possible (check if ddflow can by itself without llm - do a research for it maybe with nltk or other tools do a fuzzy search and ask the user in case of cli or agent to double check if the new data duplicates or extends pre existing one)? Add this as new phase for development with tasks after you do extensive research and propose a plan"

Research (2026-10-01, research R-dedupe-matchers): on 40 verified duplicate pairs, 17 related and 18 hard negatives from ddflow's own log, a stdlib TF-IDF cosine (code-aware tokenizer, ~10-line suffix stemmer, ids/shas masked) reranking FTS5 top-50 candidates puts the existing record in the top 3 for 95% (top 5 97.5%), finds the open task that fixes a new bug in the top 3 for 95%, at 2.5 ms median / 5.2 ms p95 per add on run_nemo_run's 6,100 records. NLTK, rapidfuzz, difflib, MinHash and scikit-learn were all no better or worse. A score cannot separate a duplicate from a different bug in the same function (hard negatives 0.43-0.64 sit inside the duplicate band), so ddflow shows candidates and the adding agent or operator answers. Benchmark scripts: the parent session's scratchpad dedup/ (corpus.py, labels.py, matchers.py, bench.py).

Decision D-no-duplicates (accepted). Task order: 1 -> 2 -> {3, 4 after B168} -> 5 -> {6, 7, 8, 9, 10} -> 11. Several tasks touch files bug-fix agents hold on 2026-10-01 (cli.py, mcp.py, api/knowledge.py, api/lifecycle.py, api/items.py, api/reporting.py, config.py): claim after those merge.
title: Nothing filed twice: every add checks for an existing record, extends it when it can, and links it when it cannot

body:
Fixes bug B9cf58aaeaa: a refused MCP ddflow_claim returns a first content block of all-null fields with the reason only in a second block. Prerequisite of B-add-dedupe-surfaces, whose 'possible duplicate' refusal must carry its candidates to the agent. Acceptance: every refusal (exit 3) over MCP leads with the reason and any structured payload; regression test fails on main.

Phase BL-no-duplicates; decision D-no-duplicates; research R-dedupe-matchers.
title: A refused MCP call returns its reason and candidates in the first result block, not a block of nulls (fixes bug B9cf58aaeaa)

body:
Commit the 40 duplicate, 17 related and 18 hard-negative pairs verified in research R-dedupe-matchers (labels.py in the research scratch), with a corpus snapshot of ddflow's records, REDACTED so tests/test_repo_is_generic.py passes (several bug texts contain LAN addresses). The test scores the engine against it and fails until B-similar-engine lands. Acceptance: fixture + test committed, redaction verified.

Phase BL-no-duplicates; decision D-no-duplicates; research R-dedupe-matchers.
title: Labelled duplicate / related / hard-negative set from the real logs, as a committed fixture and a regression test

body:
Per D-no-duplicates and R-dedupe-matchers. FTS5 picks top-50 candidates per kind from index.db; stdlib TF-IDF cosine reranks (IDF stored in index.db); without FTS5 compare against everything. [dedupe] config: on_match (ask|warn|off), show_floor 0.35, ask_threshold 0.55, max_candidates 3, min_words 8, kinds. Cross-kind candidates (a bug sees open tasks and vice versa). Flags: text names an existing id; same item. Acceptance on the evaluation set: duplicates R@3 >= 0.95; related R@5 >= 0.9; lenient precision at the ask threshold >= 0.75; hard negatives above it <= 20%; p95 < 50 ms at 6k records; same results without FTS5; no new dependency. store.py is also in B194/B-semantic-recall: keep an interface embeddings can plug into later.

Phase BL-no-duplicates; decision D-no-duplicates; research R-dedupe-matchers.

body: Fixes B9a337697c0, a regression from B-fix-merge-report (9e775b6) found by roborev job 924. merged_sha became the landing commit on the merge target; for a gitflow hotfix that merge commit is on main only, and the branch head reached develop by back-merge, so 'merge-base --is-ancestor merged_sha develop' fails and version show/pr-sync release lists drop the item. Item gains branch_head (folded from worktree.merged); services/flow.py treats an item as shipped on ref when merged_sha or branch_head is an ancestor. merge records sha = landed_after only (empty, with a warning, if the base cannot be read back) instead of silently falling back to the branch head. CLI/MCP merge payload parity test.
title: Version planning counts an item shipped on a line when its landing OR its branch head reached it (gitflow back-merge); the fold keeps worktree.merged's branch_head; merge's sha is never silently the branch head (fixes bug B9a337697c0)

body: Split from B-shared-globs (decision D-shared-globs). Evidence (home-simulator 2026-10-01): committing a merge from main in 34.8i's worktree (5301005) warned '17 staged path(s) are not covered by a lease you hold', listing main's already-merged changes. check_commit exempts only a CLEAN merge conclusion (clean_merge_conclusion); a merge with resolved conflicts stages every path main changed. Expected: during a merge (MERGE_HEAD present), drop staged paths whose index content equals the incoming parent's (MERGE_HEAD) version -- they arrive from the base, not from this item -- and check only the rest. Regression test: a worktree merges main with one conflict resolved; the hook lists only the paths that differ from MERGE_HEAD.
title: The commit hook does not list paths a merge from the base branch brought in as unleased (second half of bug B07878037ab)
